articles.title: Ce logiciel débride les Nvidia GeForce RTX 20, 30 et 40 — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Depuis quelques jours, il est possible de débrider ses cartes graphiques GeForce RTX. Alors, ne vous attendez pas à de meilleures performances en jeu. Il s’agit ici de débrider les calculs utiles pour l’IA.
Et le bridage de l’IA sur les GeForce se contourne désormais sous Windows. Le projet open source nv-uefi-unlocker, publié sur GitHub par le développeur physicsdolphin, s’exécute depuis une clé USB avant le démarrage du système et vise les RTX 20, 30 et 40, portables compris
On peut s’attendre à un gain de 65 % en calcul FP16 (un format de nombres courts très utilisé par les modèles d’IA) sur la RTX 4060 de PC portable par exemple. Fin octobre, le hack gpu-unlock-ada ne tournait que sous Linux et sur deux cartes, une RTX 4090 et une RTX 4070 Ti Super.
Sur ses GeForce, Nvidia fait tourner à mi-régime un mode de calcul des cœurs Tensor, les unités dédiées à l’IA, alors que la puce sait aller deux fois plus vite. L’outil reprend la charge utile mise au point par la communauté et l’injecte pendant la phase UEFI, celle où le micrologiciel de la carte mère tourne avant Windows et avant le pilote Nvidia. Il pousse ainsi le micrologiciel signé de Nvidia à ouvrir deux registres qui fixent la vitesse des cœurs Tensor. Puis il relit les valeurs pour vérifier que l’écriture a bien pris.
Rien n’est écrit dans le BIOS de la carte ni dans le pilote. Ce qui signifie que couper le courant suffit à tout remettre d’origine, ce qui oblige en revanche à repasser par la clé à chaque démarrage. L…

articles.title: ChatGPT : un humain sur sept l'utilise chaque semaine, quatre ans seulement après son lancement — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Pour mesurer la vitesse de diffusion des nouvelles technologies, le journaliste de données Samuel Bennett a superposé, le 12 octobre dernier sur son site The News in Data, les courbes de croissance de cinq assistants IA et des principaux réseaux sociaux à partir de leur jour de lancement respectif.
Ce graphique montre un changement d’échelle inédit : il n’a fallu qu’environ 44 mois au chatbot d’OpenAI pour réunir un milliard d’adeptes, contre 49 mois pour TikTok, 92 pour Instagram et 103 pour Facebook. À titre de comparaison, Twitter (devenu X) n’a jamais franchi ce seuil, plafonnant à 336 millions d’inscrits actifs début 2018.
Cette trajectoire hors norme a démarré dès le 30 novembre 2022. Lancé gratuitement avec le modèle GPT-3.5, l’outil avait séduit son premier million de curieux en seulement cinq jours, selon Sam Altman, le patron d’OpenAI.
La cadence s’est ensuite nettement accélérée en 2026 : après avoir revendiqué 900 millions d’utilisateurs hebdomadaires fin février dans un billet intitulé « Scaling AI for everyone » (l’IA pour tout le monde, en somme), l’entreprise a franchi le milliard en août, avant de grimper à 1,2 milliard fin septembre. Concrètement, environ un être humain sur sept utilise désormais le service chaque semaine. Dans un rapport publié le 30 juin et présenté comme « un nouveau regard sur l’adoption mondiale de l’IA », OpenAI précise d’ailleurs que plus de la moitié de sa base active interagit aujourd’hui dans une autre langue que l’anglais.

articles.title: Après la RAM, le stockage et les processeurs, l'IA fait grimper le prix de ce composant essentiel — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Après avoir fait flamber le prix de la RAM et poussé Intel à augmenter encore le prix de ses processeurs pour PC portables, la ruée vers l’IA s’attaque à la carte sur laquelle ces puces sont soudées. Dans une enquête publiée le 27 octobre, Nikkei Asia rapporte qu’un fabricant de PC taïwanais paie le stratifié cuivré au moins 12 fois plus cher qu’en juillet.
Cette feuille de fibre de verre et de résine recouverte de cuivre (CCL en anglais) sert de base à chaque circuit imprimé, ou PCB. Et des PCB, il y en a dans tout ce qui contient une puce : carte mère, carte graphique, barrette de mémoire, smartphone, console.
Ce chiffre vient d’une seule entreprise et ne vaut pas forcément pour toutes les références de stratifié. Mais les délais, eux, s’allongent nettement. D’après les industriels interrogés par Nikkei Asia, certaines commandes de PCB demandent jusqu’à 30 mois, deux fois plus qu’il y a un an. Une carte commandée aujourd’hui pourrait donc n’arriver qu’à la fin 2028.
Plus inquiétant encore, l’un des plus gros fournisseurs mondiaux de stratifié aurait un carnet de commandes plein jusqu’en 2030, alors qu’il prévoit de tripler sa capacité d’ici 2028.
Les serveurs IA passent devant
Les serveurs IA réclament des cartes bien plus complexes et rapportent bien plus aux fabricants, donc ils sont servis en priorité. Une carte de serveur IA empile des dizaines de couches de stratifié spécial, ce qui mobilise bien plus de matière et de temps machine qu’une carte mère de PC.

articles.title: Jackery made its portable power stations even smaller
articles.summary:
Jackery announced a new portable power station that uses the safer and longer-lasting lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries the company first introduced in 2023. But what makes the new Explorer 100D stand out is that it’s Jackery’s smallest power station to date, measuring only 4.6 by 3.4 by 3.4 inches and weighing just 1.87 pounds. Its size and 96Wh (30,000mAh) of battery capacity means you can squeeze it into your carry-on and power multiple devices during a long flight.
Jackery made its portable power stations even smaller
The new Jackery Explorer 100D puts a longer lasting lithium iron phosphate battery in the palm of your hand.
The Jackery Explorer 100D will be available starting November 15th through Walmart for $99. The power station is already available from Costco if you don’t want to wait, but only in a two-pack for $179.99. You can definitely find smaller and cheaper 30,000mAh portable chargers, but the LFP cells in the 100D are “engineered for up to 8 years of regular use,” according to Jackery, with a 3,000 charge cycle lifespan, so it should easily outlast competing products that use more common lithium-ion battery cells.
Although the 100D is considerably smaller and lighter than Jackery’s other portable power stations, the company still includes an integrated handle and offers an optional shoulder strap for carrying it around. On the front, you’ll find a pair of 140W USB-C ports, plus an additional 18W USB-A port, but the 100D maxes out at 158W of total output…

articles.title: Overwatch aura-t-il une campagne narrative un jour ? Ce n'est pas gagné
articles.summary:
La saga Overwatch a connu un reboot salvateur en février 2026, en abandonnant le chiffre 2 et en revenant à des fondamentaux plus en phase avec les attentes des fans. Ceux qui espèrent encore voir arriver la campagne narrative ambitieuse promise avec le second épisode risquent d’être déçus.
À l’occasion d’une table ronde à laquelle a assisté TheGamer, Aaron Keller a répondu à la question des contenus PvE (joueurs contre ordinateur). Dans ses propos rapportés le 31 octobre, il ne ferme pas totalement la porte. En revanche, un mode histoire à grande échelle n’est pas d’actualité, faute de ressources mais aussi d’intérêt de la communauté.
Les fans d’Overwatch veulent-ils vraiment des missions PvE ?
Aaron Keller avance d’abord l’argument du manque d’engagement des joueuses et des joueurs pour ces missions événementielles. Il revient sur les missions narratives déjà sorties : « Quand vous regardez les campagnes que nous avons proposées, je pense que bien qu’elles aient suscité beaucoup d’enthousiasme et fait progresser l’histoire, elles n’ont pas vraiment été jouées comme nous le souhaitions. » Sur Reddit, on lit çà et là que Le Règne de Talon, l’arc narrartif en cours, ne déchaîne pas les passions non plus.
Selon Aaron Keller, ce type de contenu attire du monde au lancement, puis l’intérêt retombe très vite.

Cette location longue durée à loyer réduit grâce à une prime, réservée aux ménages modestes, a ouvert les commandes de sa troisième édition le 16 juillet 2026, et les voitures commandées cet été arrivent maintenant chez leurs conducteurs.

articles.title: Fans Rebuild Valve's Scrapped Portal Prequel "F-Stop" From Three Separate Leaks
articles.summary:
Monday, November 2nd 2026
Fans Rebuild Valve's Scrapped Portal Prequel "F-Stop" From Three Separate Leaks
F-Stop, the Portal prequel Valve canceled in 2007, is now playable after the community stitched it together from several leaks. Most of its assets were already sitting in the gigantic 12 TB Steam2 archive that leaked in August, but that dump didn't include the game's source code or its mapsrc data, Valve's folder for map source files. Those two missing pieces showed up on the Valve Cut Content project's Discord server over the past few days, where the team verified the map files before everything was merged into one build. It isn't fully complete, as some textures and dialogue are still missing, but YouTube playthroughs suggest it's largely stable, and the campaign wraps up in under an hour. Getting a copy yourself is another matter, since the Discord server apparently went invite-only after all the attention.
F-Stop came out of what Gabe Newell later called the Directed Design Experiments, a three-month stretch where Valve split into five teams, each building its own prototype. Its central idea is an Aperture Science camera that photographs an object so you can place it elsewhere to solve puzzles, a concept the 2023 game Viewfinder later explored. Valve staff apparently liked it, but playtesters were less impressed. It was shelved, and some of its dialogue, characters, and mechanics were reworked into Portal 2. articles.title: Des panneaux publicitaires diffusent du porno en pleine rue après une cyberattaque internationale
articles.summary:
Sur l’axe du 26-Juillet, à Gizeh, des automobilistes se sont arrêtés pour filmer un écran publicitaire géant sur lequel des pirates diffusaient une vidéo pornographique. Les auteurs de l’attaque affirment avoir pris le contrôle d’écrans LED dans plusieurs autres pays, de la Malaisie au Brésil.
Sur les images, les pirates avaient incrusté quatre pseudonymes et l’adresse de leur canal Telegram, Leakers$. En Malaisie, le conseil municipal de Kluang, dans l’État de Johor, a fait éteindre tous les écrans publics touchés, et la police a ouvert une enquête après la plainte d’un homme de 42 ans. Il avait reçu des captures d’écran et des vidéos de la scène sur WhatsApp. Au Brésil, à Campo Maior, l’entreprise Ferreira & Ferreira a coupé son panneau LED installé près de la BR-343, porté plainte et présenté ses excuses aux habitants. Le groupe assure avoir piraté des écrans en Irak et en Chine, mais personne n’a pu le vérifier de façon indépendante.
Une faille dans le logiciel de diffusion des écrans LED
Les pirates ont exploité une faille du programme chargé d’envoyer les vidéos aux écrans LED, et non les panneaux un par un, a expliqué un représentant du groupe au site d’information égyptien The Cairo Report. Avec un balayage automatique d’environ deux heures, les quatre membres de l’équipe disent avoir repéré des milliers de systèmes accessibles depuis de simples pages web, sans la moindre protection. « Après l’avoir exploitée, nous avons obtenu l’accès à des systèmes d’affichage dans …

articles.title: Anthropic met à jour Claude pour l’empêcher de recréer des jeux vidéo existants
articles.summary:
Demandez à Claude Code de refaire Fallout ou GTA V sous un autre nom, et l’assistant de programmation d’Anthropic refusera la tâche. L’entreprise a ajouté deux phrases aux instructions de son modèle Opus 5.5, après une série de jeux célèbres recréés par des fans avec son IA et publiés en ligne.
Chasm, un utilisateur de X, a repéré la nouvelle règle fin octobre dans les instructions qu’Anthropic transmet à Claude Code depuis ses serveurs. Claude doit continuer à construire des jeux originaux ou inspirés d’un genre, notamment à partir des dessins et des ressources graphiques de l’utilisateur. Il doit en revanche refuser « la recréation d’un jeu existant précis, même renommée ou présentée comme originale ». « Utiliser Claude pour enfreindre la propriété intellectuelle va à l’encontre de notre politique d’utilisation », souligne Addy Osmani, membre de l’équipe technique d’Anthropic, qui a confirmé le changement sur X que vous pourrez voir ci-dessous. Mais Claude refuse aussi certaines demandes de développeurs qui n’ont jamais voulu copier un jeu.
Fallout et GTA V reproduits en quelques jours avec l’IA

articles.title: Plus besoin de solliciter l'IA à chaque étape, DeepSeek expérimente un agent de programmation plus autonome
articles.summary:
Chez DeepSeek, un agent de programmation suit les discussions de groupe des développeurs et soumet sur GitHub la correction d’un bug signalé, avant même que quelqu’un la lui réclame. L’entreprise chinoise met en libre accès un prototype de cet assistant, avec l’ambition de rivaliser avec le Claude Code d’Anthropic.
Les développeurs qui font travailler plusieurs agents d’IA à la fois doivent passer d’une session à l’autre, en se souvenant de ce qu’ils ont demandé à chacun. D’après les observations de l’équipe Harness de DeepSeek, un utilisateur suit rarement plus de trois à cinq sessions actives simultanément. Avec son Super-agent, l’entreprise cache toutes ces sessions derrière un interlocuteur unique. Les développeurs échangent avec lui dans leur messagerie et sur GitHub, et n’interviennent plus que pour trancher ou valider un résultat. Le reste du temps, l’agent travaille en silence.
Une demande dans la messagerie, une pull request en retour
Les développeurs installent le Super-agent dans Harness. DeepSeek distribue cet environnement d’agents en open source, sous licence MIT, afin de concurrencer Claude Code et les autres assistants de programmation américains. L’entreprise a réuni environ 100 milliards de yuans, soit 15 milliards de dollars, lors de son dernier tour de table, en vue d’une introduction en Bourse.

articles.title: Hubble et James Webb ont magnifiquement photographié un chat de poussière dans la nébuleuse de la Carène
articles.summary:
L'Agence spatiale européenne a dévoilé de nouvelles images de la nébuleuse de la Tête de Chat, captées par les télescopes Hubble et James Webb dans la nébuleuse de la Carène. Trois regards complémentaires sur une pouponnière d’étoiles.
Les télescopes Hubble et James Webb ont braqué leurs instruments sur la nébuleuse de la Tête de Chat, une colonne de gaz et de poussière située à environ 7 500 années-lumière de la Terre. L'Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) a publié le 29 octobre trois images aussi magnifiques qu'impressionnantes de cette région, l'une en lumière visible, les deux autres en infrarouge. Un chat de poussière sculpté par les étoiles
Ce long pilier de poussière sombre doit son allure féline à un voisinage particulièrement agité. Selon l'ESA, sa silhouette aurait été sculptée au fil du temps par les étoiles massives de la Carène, des astres bien plus lourds et plus chauds que notre Soleil. Ensemble, ils balaient peu à peu le gaz et la poussière alentour, un peu comme un jet de sable décape une façade. Les zones les moins denses s'envolent, tandis que les plus compactes résistent et dessinent ce pilier félin. Du moins pour l'instant.

articles.title: How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85%
articles.summary:
How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85%
When I last wrote about our DNS propagation pipeline in 2022, the Zone Builder received about 250 DNS record changes per second. Today it receives about 700, nearly three times as many, plus about 100 other events, such as zone setting changes. However, the number of events was never the real problem. The problem was the kind of work some of those events needed, and how that work grows with the size of a zone. Some zones now hold more than 20 million records, and we expect them to keep growing toward hundreds of millions.
Each event starts a clock that measures how long it takes us to turn that change into data our authoritative DNS servers can use. We call that work a build. A build reads the current database state, converts it into the format used at the edge, and writes any changes to Quicksilver.
In 2022, per-record builds were 150 times faster than full builds on average. On a test zone with one million records, per-record builds were 4,250 times faster. We ended that post with the obvious next step: do the same thing for zone settings.
Why doesn't the Zone Builder just rebuild the setting that changed?
It should, and that is where we ended up. However, proving when it was safe took most of the work. A record event identifies what changed. On Kubernetes, each framework encodes that information differently. JobSet, LeaderWorkerSet, and other custom resources often require separate adapters before a tool can interpret and manage them.
NVIDIA Workload Map provides a common description of Kubernetes workload structure that users can reuse across frameworks. As part of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, Workload Map enables integrated schedulers, controllers, and platforms to interpret supported workload types without maintaining separate framework-specific parsing code.

On Kubernetes, a real workload is rarely a single pod. A distributed training job or a multi-node inference server is a small tree of resources: groups of pods, each with a role, a replica count, a pod template, and a status that depends on the workload type.

The agentic web is here
With the rise of personal AI assistants, the internet isn't just for humans anymore.
In 2001, a decade after he invented the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision. Together with two colleagues, he published an article in the magazine Scientific American in which he outlined what he called the “Semantic Web”: an internet designed to be navigated by autonomous software agents that could address our every need, without requiring us to muck about with browsers and search engines ourselves.
To illustrate what this might look like, Berners-Lee and his colleagues told a story about a pair of siblings who use their agents to automatically research and book physical therapy appointments for their mother, making sure they would be covered by insurance and fit their busy calendars.
At the turn of the millennium, this vision seemed far-fetched: Google had only been online for a couple of years, and most people were still on dial-up connections. But a quarter-century on, the dream of autonomous software agents that use the internet and carry out tasks for us has finally been realized. New tools such as Meta’s blockbuster Muse agent, OpenAI’s Dots, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet are being given access to people’s email inboxes and bank accounts, Meanwhile, in a series of worrying incidents, agents created by OpenAI broke free of their sandboxes and caused havoc online.

articles.title: Canadian banks blocking AI agents amid security concerns
articles.summary:
Canada’s biggest banks, including RBC, TD, CIBC, and others, are blocking AI agents from accessing online bank accounts over security concerns.
The decision comes as major U.S. banks, like Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo, and others, reportedly detected unauthorized activity from AI agents on customer accounts, with some agents apparently taking actions that are independent of user instructions.
Earlier this year, tech companies launched AI agent tools that they claim can take action for users and help them complete tasks. Meta’s Muse garnered the most attention, but ChatGPT maker OpenAI wasn’t far behind with the launch of its own agent tool, Dots. articles.title: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
articles.summary:
Sponsored
Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
Why rationing agentic coding backfires, and what to measure instead.
Provided byHPE
When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt. The more useful the agent becomes, the more calls it makes. With per-token pricing, the workflows creating the most value can also become the most expensive.
The financial pressure is already visible. Uber reportedly exhausted its entire 2026 AI budget by April after expanding its use of Claude Code. GitHub Copilot moved from flat-rate pricing to metered credits. Gartner predicts that AI coding token costs will surpass average developer salaries by 2028.
The natural response is rationing usage caps, seat limits, and approvals before developers launch agents. But blanket limits can restrict the workflows delivering value. They also optimize the wrong number. Cost per token measures consumption, not results. Some spending reflects waste, including retries and runaway loops. Some represents the work of shipping software. A meter cannot distinguish them, and neither can a spending cap.
Measure the software that ships

articles.title: Xbox’s former COO has ‘serious concerns’ about her abrupt departure
articles.summary:
Xbox’s former chief operating officer, Helen Chiang, suddenly left Microsoft less than two weeks ago after being promoted into the role in July. I wrote in my Notepad newsletter last week that it seemed very weird for Chiang to suddenly depart Microsoft after 21 years with a surprisingly short memo from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. Now, Chiang says she has “serious concerns” about how she was treated.
Xbox’s former COO has ‘serious concerns’ about her abrupt departure
Helen Chiang is setting the record straight on her sudden exit from Microsoft.
In a lengthy LinkedIn post — entitled “clarity is kindness,” a reference to Sharma’s WSJ profile — Chiang doesn’t dispute that she was fired, but she doesn’t say why she was let go. Eurogamer reported last month that Chiang had been “terminated for policy violations,” but she says this is “not accurate.”
Chiang denies unfounded rumors that speculated she was leaking confidential information, or that she left to join a competitor. It’s clear the decision to leave Xbox was out of her hands. “You don’t spend two decades somewhere without developing a deep loyalty to the people, teams, and businesses you’ve helped build,” says Chiang. “Xbox was never just another stop in my career. My end game was always to keep building here.”

articles.title: Cohere pledges to invest $4 billion into R&D, create 1,500 jobs
articles.summary:
At the end of last week, the Government of Canada announced a $1.6 billion investment in Toronto-based AI company Cohere. Following that announcement, Cohere has provided some updates on its larger plans for Canada.
Most notably, Cohere says it’s investing over $4 billion in R&D and AI infrastructure through 2031. The company says this will create over 1,500 jobs, 1,000 of which will focus on “AI research, engineering, product development and other advanced technical disciplines.”
The feds’ investment in Cohere comes as part of the company’s wider $7 billion fundraising round. Altogether, this will put Cohere’s valuation at about $36 billion, which the government says makes it the largest AI company outside of the U.S. and China. In a statement last week, Prime Minister Mark Carney said these Cohere investments will help produce “affordable, secure, sovereign AI, built in Canada for the benefit of Canadians.”
However, there’s naturally been a lot of scrutiny into all of this news. For one, the Cohere investment is believed to be the largest-ever federal equity investment in a single private tech company. And yet, there’s still many questions surrounding the terms of the deal, including what degree of control the feds have over Cohere.
And on a wider level, there’s a lot of apprehension regarding AI companies in general. Not only is there a huge lack of regulation across the board, including in Canada, but data centres also carry significant energy, water, and land costs.

articles.title: OpenAI's plan to make data centers less hated: Rename them "compute campuses"
articles.summary:
WTF?! With all the negativity associated with the facilities, it's fair to say that the term data center has become a dirty word. OpenAI is well aware of this, which is why the company wants to call them something else: compute campuses.
An OpenAI spokesperson told Business Insider about the rebrand. "Compute campuses better describes the scale and role of the infrastructure we're building for AI," the spokesperson said. "These are long-term investments in computing, energy infrastructure and skilled work."
It seems that the ChatGPT maker is trying to appeal to those living near data centers by convincing them that they are part of this beautiful AI revolution.
"We want the communities hosting that infrastructure to help shape it and share in the opportunities it creates," the OpenAI spokesperson added.
Whether the locals angry about the noise, pollution, falling house prices, increased water consumption, and higher electricity bills will care about this shaping and sharing remains to be seen.
Several companies have tried offering incentives to local residents to appease them (or convince them not to sue), but even handing over thousands of dollars isn't enough to tempt many people. A survey from earlier this year found more Americans would rather live next to a nuclear power plant than a data center.

articles.title: EUA planejam bloquear ligações de operadoras chinesas • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
EUA planejam bloquear ligações de operadoras chinesas
Proposta da FCC cita riscos de golpes telefônicos e à segurança nacional. Embaixada da China diz que ação prejudicaria comércio entre países.
Os Estados Unidos podem bloquear ligações de telefonias chinesas para números registrados no país. A Federal Communications Commission (FCC), órgão análogo à Anatel, afirma que a decisão seria motivada para combater golpes via discagem automática, conhecidas como robocalls. A proposta será votada em 19 de novembro e pode banir o acesso direto de companhias como a China Mobile, China Telecom e China Unicom.
A FCC já havia impedido essas companhias de oferecerem serviços de telecomunicações no país. Além das telefonias em si, a nova medida também pretende barrar provedores com serviços via IP que utilizem roteadores e outros equipamentos de Huawei e ZTE, classificados como um risco à segurança nacional.
O presidente Donald Trump tem adotado uma postura mais agressiva na taxação e proibição de eletrônicos chineses. Em resposta, a Embaixada da China em Washington criticou os planos anunciados pelo FCC e afirmou que a medida poderia prejudicar ainda mais o comércio entre os dois países.
A FCC afirma que o banimento dessas ligações seria uma forma de combater golpes telefônicos no país. Segundo o presidente do órgão, Brendan Carr, a decisão vai “reforçar a primeira linha de defesa contra atores maliciosos e robocallers ilegais”. articles.title: FBI Flags Over 600 Addresses Tied to North Korea’s Binance Heist
articles.summary:
The FBI has formally blamed North Korean state-sponsored hackers for the record-breaking Binance cryptocurrency heist and is asking the crypto industry to help stop the stolen funds from being laundered.
The attack was conducted on October 29. Hackers emptied Binance hot wallets on multiple blockchains, moving most of the funds out within roughly 20 minutes. Binance estimates the impact at roughly $6.3 billion, the largest crypto theft on record.
Within hours, blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis linked the attack to the North Korean group TraderTraitor. Binance initially said the intrusion may have started with a DevOps engineer’s compromised laptop, and pledged to cover all losses.
The FBI released its attribution on October 31, two days after the theft.
“The FBI, together with partners at the USSS and IRS-CI, has observed TraderTraitor actors converting stolen assets primarily into Ethereum (ETH). It is expected these assets will then be further laundered by converting them using DeFi and instant swap services as they prepare them for further laundering stages,” the agency said.
The alert names 608 Ethereum addresses, 19 Bitcoin addresses and one Solana address that currently hold, or previously held, proceeds of the theft.
Together with the Secret Service and IRS-CI, the FBI called on THORChain node operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services and blockchain analytics firms to refuse transactions linked to these addresses.

articles.title: Vigilancia con drones y multas de hasta 45.000 euros: así controla la policía de Vilanova de Arousa (Pontevedra) a los vecinos que tiran mal la basura
articles.summary:
En Vilanova de Arousa (Pontevedra), la Policía Local también usa drones para controlar los vertidos ilegales. Los agentes persiguen a los ciudadanos que dejan muebles o escombros en la vía pública. Se les advierte de sanciones que pueden llegar a ser de 45.000 euros. Pero esa cifra no es una multa acreditada por un error de contenedor.
Se trata de una búsqueda de posibles orígenes. Cuando encuentran algún residuo, buscan con el dron si hay alguna obra cercana. Según explica uno de los agentes, “el infractor suele estar más cerca de lo que parece”. Algunas de las conductas que han detectado son, por ejemplo, dejar somieres en la acera o tirar pintura en zonas verdes. Para advertir de la vigilancia también han puesto carteles.
Este tipo de vigilancia aérea ya está registrada desde agosto de 2025. En ese momento se hablaba de un protocolo policial para combatir los vertidos que incluía este tipo de vigilancia junto a registros de grabación y alerta ciudadana para detectar responsables.
Las sanciones dependen de la infracción
Los agentes hablan de sanciones de 200 o 500 euros, hasta 45.000 en función de la peligrosidad. Es importante destacar que en este caso estamos ante situaciones diferentes a la de error de contenedor (por ejemplo, en el caso de dejar residuos de reforma o bien de sustancias peligrosas).

articles.summary:
Published November 1, 2026
The problem with putting an African fintech on Wall Street
A smartphone displaying OPay’s EaseMoni loan interface, advertising loan limits of up to ₦3 million ($2,234). Image source: TechCabal
OPay had everything an IPO is supposed to deliver: a $4 billion valuation, a $304 million share sale, backing from SoftBank and a ceremonial opening bell at the New York Stock Exchange. On October 30, its executives stood on the exchange floor as the Nigerian payments company prepared to become one of Africa’s biggest technology listings in the US. By the following morning, the deal was dead. Not a single share had traded.
OPay had priced 16 million American Depositary Shares at $19 each, the bottom of its marketed range. By 2 pm, indicative bids had fallen to between $16.25 and $16.75. The NYSE halted trading in its shares with news pending at 3.30 pm. The next morning, the underwriting syndicate walked away.
OPay described the decision as an abundance of caution over an inquiry in an undisclosed foreign jurisdiction, which it called “immaterial to its core business operations”.
This is an awkward explanation for a company whose bankers had just abandoned its biggest capital markets transaction. Whatever the inquiry concerned, it was material enough to stop a $4 billion listing. articles.title: Making Kubernetes AI-Ready for NVIDIA Vera Rubin on Day One | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Configuring and optimizing Kubernetes for new GPU hardware such as NVIDIA Vera Rubin is complex and error-prone. Drivers, kernels, runtimes, networking, operators, and schedulers must work together, with settings tuned to the hardware and workload. Small mismatches can prevent workloads from running or limit performance.
The NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR)—part of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform—simplifies this work by capturing tuned configurations in reusable recipes, generating bundles for existing deployment tools, and validating the running cluster. It will help Kubernetes environments be ready for NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 compute trays on Day 1.
Overall, the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform brings together technologies to help the ecosystem design, build, and operate more efficient AI factories, including open source, modular software components purpose-built to support multi-tenant operations and scaling.
Configuring new hardware architecture in a cloud-native stack requires plumbing updates from the lowest-level bindings all the way up to the orchestration layer. It is still early days for Vera Rubin.
This post covers what changes if you run NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 today, what has been validated on early hardware access using NVIDIA GPU Operator and the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) driver with Vera Rubin support. It also shows how AICR brings these components together in a configuration that platform teams can reproduce and verify.

Seamoretech, a Porto-based CleanTech startup that converts desalination brine into freshwater and critical minerals, has secured €1.1 million in the first closing of its Seed round.
The round saw participation from Rypples, 7Seas Capital, and Crédito Agrícola, bringing together investors with experience in OceanTech and ClimateTech industries. The first closing has also brought the total amount raised to €3 million.
“We are entering Seamoretech’s next phase with a clear ambition: to scale our technology, accelerate our market entry, produce freshwater at a lower cost, and establish a European reference in critical raw materials recovery, while helping protect marine ecosystems,” said Sofia Delgado, CEO and co-founder of Seamoretech.
Founded in 2021 by Delgado and Eva Sousa as a spin-off of the University of Porto’s Faculty of Engineering (FEUP), Seamoretech tackles brine, the highly concentrated saline waste stream that industries have long treated as a liability and discarded into the ocean. The startup’s proprietary brine valorisation technology recovers purified freshwater and high-value minerals, including magnesium, calcium, copper, and lithium, from the waste stream.
The technology relies on a containerised, plug-and-play system that uses a forward osmosis process to achieve Zero Liquid Discharge, meaning nothing is returned to the ocean. articles.title: OpenAI’s new shared usage limit pits ChatGPT against Codex
articles.summary:
OpenAI’s new shared usage limit pits ChatGPT against Codex
OpenAI has revealed plans to combine usage allowances across ChatGPT and Codex, as part of a broader effort to integrate its conversational AI and agentic capabilities into a single experience.
In a help article quietly published over the weekend, the company confirmed the changes will take effect “starting in December,” affecting Plus, Pro and Business subscribers. Under the new system, ChatGPT conversations and Codex tasks will draw from a common pool of tokens, with more demanding models and complex tasks consuming a greater share — though OpenAI has yet to disclose how generous the combined allowance will be.
Instant chat, ChatGPT’s faster-response mode for everyday questions and tasks, will be exempt.
OpenAI’s products come together
The changes are the latest step in OpenAI’s efforts to bring its growing collection of AI products under one roof.
In July, the company launched ChatGPT Work, an agentic tool built on its Codex coding technology that allows users to delegate complex tasks, such as researching topics, analysing data and producing documents, presentations and spreadsheets. The idea was to extend the capabilities of Codex beyond software development, allowing knowledge workers to use AI agents for everyday business tasks.

Agentic engineering intelligence with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
When a qualified aerospace component goes obsolete or hits a long lead time, an engineer spends days cross-referencing specifications across vendor datasheets, interface control documents (ICDs), and qualification records before documenting a substitution justification for review. An incorrect substitution on a flight-critical component can cause mission failure, yet the evidence trail behind each decision is often spread across email and undocumented institutional knowledge, so there is no formal, repeatable package for a reviewer to check.
A previous post, Manufacturing intelligence with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings, showed how the model retrieves answers locked inside engineering diagrams, thermal plots, and datasheet charts that text-only pipelines miss. This post picks up where that retrieval work left off, putting those capabilities inside a multi-agent system that assembles substitution evidence, from retrieval to a drafted assessment.
In this post, we show how to build a multi-agent engineering assistant that cuts the manual cross-referencing behind part substitution evaluation using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings, and the open source Strands Agents SDK. articles.title: Ces 319 extensions Chrome ont espionné des millions d'internautes pendant 10 ans
articles.summary:
Des chercheurs de l’entreprise de cybersécurité Socket ont identifié un réseau de 319 extensions Chrome qui détournent les recherches des internautes. Ce système serait actif depuis dix ans et aurait potentiellement touché 13,4 millions d’utilisateurs.
Des extensions Chrome destinées à enregistrer vos requêtes
De prime abord, ces extensions Chrome, destinées à détourner les recherches des internautes, semblent inoffensives en se présentant comme des convertisseurs de DFD, des outils de recherche de manuels, des moteurs de recherche sécurisés ou encore des assistants IA de recherche. Mais en réalité, elles ont un double objectif. D’une part, les requêtes saisies dans Chrome transitent sur des serveurs proxy contrôlés par les opérateurs des extensions. D’autre part, ces extensions redirigent l’internaute vers Yahoo ou Bing afin que les pirates bénéficient de commissions de parrainage, étant donné que du trafic est généré sur ces deux moteurs de recherche concurrents de Google.
Pour être plus précis, les pirates exploitent un paramètre de Chrome qui permet à une extension de remplacer le moteur de recherche par défaut. Par ailleurs, il faut noter que certaines de ces extensions ne demandent aucune autorisation particulière de la part de l’internaute.
Comment éviter tout risque ?

articles.title: Synology warns of C3RB3R ransomware attacks targeting NAS devices
articles.summary:
Taiwanese network-attached storage (NAS) appliance maker Synology warned customers to update their devices immediately due to a surge in C3RB3r ransomware attacks.
The company urged users to enable automatic updates and upgrade the DiskStation Manager (DSM) software running on their NAS devices to the latest version to protect their data.
"Synology has identified threat actors exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to target devices running outdated versions of DSM. These attacks aim to encrypt data and extort ransom," it said in a Thursday advisory.
"Synology strongly urges all users running vulnerable versions to update DSM immediately to protect their systems. Synology also recommends enabling automatic updates to keep DSM up to date at all times."
A Synology spokesperson was not immediately available when BleepingComputer reached out for more information on these C3RB3r ransomware attacks.
While Synology has yet to share which vulnerability is being exploited in these ongoing attacks, it linked to a November 2024 security advisory with information about patches released for vulnerabilities allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code (CVE-2024-10441), read files (CVE-2024-50629), and write files (CVE-2024-10445) on unpatched devices.
Synology users are advised to immediately block access to the management web interface from the Internet and update their DSM software to block attackers' attempts to hack and encrypt their devices.

articles.title: Niger-based Likita Care wins 2026 Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
Niger-based medical monitoring startup Likita Care has won the 2026 Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation, taking home GBP50,000 (US$67,000).
Delivered by the Royal Academy of Engineering, the Africa Prize is the continent’s biggest engineering prize. Finalists were selected from a cohort of 16 entrepreneurs who completed an eight-month training and mentoring programme.
Founded by Mamane Kabirou Ousseini, the first engineer from Niger to participate in and win the prize, Likita Care builds locally manufactured monitoring devices that can be maintained and repaired in Niger, addressing the frequent breakdown of imported equipment in resource-limited hospitals.
The platform combines connected hardware, clinical software and an AI module that interprets vital signs in real time, supporting patient, cardiac and prenatal monitoring. More than 70 units have been deployed across five medical centres in Niger.
“Winning the Africa Prize is a dream come true,” said Ousseini. The startup will use the funding to commercialise in Niger and prepare for expansion into neighbouring West African markets.
Three runners-up each received GBP10,000 (US$13,500 – South Africa’s Pee-Cycling, a urine-to-fertiliser recovery system; Kenya’s MoyoECG, a portable heart monitor; and Kenya’s Renal Roads, a mobile dialysis clinic. Ghana’s Fusion Wind Turbine won the GBP5,000 (US$6,500) One-to-Watch Award.

articles.title: 5 Dinge, die du diese Woche wissen musst: Wie KI auch für gute Zwecke genutzt werden kann
articles.summary:
5 Dinge, die du diese Woche wissen musst: Wie KI auch für gute Zwecke genutzt werden kann
Vieles am Aufkommen und der rasanten Verbreitung von generativer KI wirkt dystopisch. Das liegt nicht nur daran, dass Filme wie Terminator schon seit Jahrzehnten unseren Blick auf diese Technologie mitprägen: KI ist unser Feind. Und es ist ja auch was dran. Zuletzt machten schließlich immer wieder Meldungen die Runde, dass KI aus ihrer vermeintlichen sicheren Umgebung ausgebrochen ist und andere Systeme attackiert hat. Doch es geht auch anders. KI kann für einen guten Zweck eingesetzt werden und gerade für Non-Profits hilfreich sein.

articles.title: Putting AI To The Test
articles.summary:
Who verifies the verifier? This is the age-old question for anyone involved in the verification of semiconductor systems. Who verifies AI?
There are an increasing number of new EDA companies these days, and this is great news. The industry needs some new vitality, new thought leaders, people willing to take risks. The same goes for established companies that cannot go outside their existing comfort zone while meeting next quarter’s financial goals. But sometimes, new startups forget the risks associated with semiconductor design. While they may be able to point to an improvement in time to market, or meeting better performance goals, they fail to understand how small that particular step is in the whole process.
Today, a number of companies want us to believe that AI can do everything. Some point the way to automating design, others to verification, and some even claim it can do both at the same time, from the same source material. No, it can’t. While some of it may be possible in the future, it is far from that point today.
What many of them fail to do is show proof. One example, one design, one piece of IP is not proof. When verifying any new tool or methodology, you always need to hold back a test set to apply at the end. In this case, with AI, it has to be something it has never seen before, never been trained on. That is the only thing that can provide a fair, unbiased result. As soon as you tweak your tool to do well on that test case, it is no longer a true test.

Cuando se grabó el vídeo, llevaban más de tres años viviendo en el campo y tenían cuatro hijos. Allí organizaban la crianza a su manera: “Nuestros hijos no van a la escuela, sino que los educamos en casa”, explica ella.
“No había un propósito vital en nuestra vida”, cuenta Sandra, que recuerda las discusiones y unas dinámicas familiares que no terminaban de funcionar. Una escapada de tres días a la montaña les dio un respiro y les hizo plantearse qué querían cambiar. “Nos dimos cuenta de que no necesitamos tanto”, resume José.
El primer destino fue una finca familiar en Jaén, que había pasado de la abuela de José a su madre. La localizaron con Google Maps y viajaron para conocerla. Tracked as CVE-2026-97229, this vulnerability stems from an integer overflow weakness and was discovered in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses and evaluates regular expressions in pipeline configuration files.
"GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation," the company explained on October 12 when it released security patches to address the security issue in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8.

On Friday, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed that attackers have begun exploiting the flaw in the wild and added CVE-2026-97229 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, ordering federal agencies to secure their servers by Sunday.

articles.title: Polymarket Returns $3.9 Million to Traders as DebugBear Cites DNS Hijack

Polymarket says it is returning $3.9 million to traders following last week’s supply chain attack. Website performance monitoring firm DebugBear, meanwhile, has disclosed that its DNS records were compromised.
On October 29, the prediction market halted trading on its international platform after users reported unauthorized withdrawals. Hudson Rock researchers linked the activity to malicious JavaScript served from a DebugBear address that Polymarket’s site loaded.
The script targeted logged-in traders. It checked their portfolios, and then either dumped positions or shifted assets to a wallet chosen by the attacker. The code read credential-related data stored in the browser, but Hudson Rock saw no evidence of it sending passwords, seed phrases or private keys back to the attacker. Instead, it piggybacked on the trading permissions of the open session.
In an October 30 update, Polymarket said 726 wallets were affected. At that point, all but 37 had been made whole, and the rest were being paid once their details were checked.
Polymarket is also covering traders hurt by the trading halt or whose positions were sold or transferred by the malicious script, paying out $1.19 million across roughly 5,500 wallets. Together with the roughly $2.7 million stolen directly, that brings the payout to $3.9 million.

articles.title: An internet tax that would charge by the gigabyte just squeaked through France's lower house
articles.summary:
WTF?! These days, moving a gigabyte of data across the internet usually costs companies well under a cent. France, however, wants them to pay several times that just in tax. Lawmakers there narrowly voted on Friday to charge content providers 5.5 cents for every gigabyte they send to French users – though the measure still has a long way to go before it becomes law.
Socialist deputy Laurent Lhardit's amendment passed the National Assembly by just 11 votes to 10. In fact, only 35 of the chamber's 577 deputies were even in the room at the time. Both the government and the budget's own rapporteur had advised against it, too.
If it survives, subscribers wouldn't be billed directly. Instead, ISPs like Orange, SFR, Bouygues Telecom and Free would tally how much data reaches their customers from each sender. Content providers would then owe €0.055 per gigabyte. That bill would be capped at 15% of French revenue or 2% of global revenue.
All told, Lhardit's group expects the tax to raise €10 billion a year. That figure leans on telecom regulator Arcep's estimate that about 200 billion gigabytes flow to French subscribers annually. Roughly half of that traffic comes from just five companies – Google, Meta, Amazon, Netflix and Akamai.

Artificial Intelligence
Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI
You built a shopping assistant on a frontier model, and it works. A shopper asks for “a black waist bag under twenty dollars from a shop with at least 4.5 stars,” and the agent searches the catalog, inspects candidates, checks the constraints, and commits to a recommendation. But what does that interaction actually cost? An agentic assistant is not one model call, it is a loop: search, read results, refine, verify, decide. A single completed task can be multiple calls to that frontier model, and you pay for every one, on every shopper. At production scale, that per-task cost compounds, erodes the project’s ROI, and stops the project from shipping.
One way to make an agentic application more efficient is to use a smaller model, which is faster to respond and more cost-effective to host. The catch is quality: a smaller model usually falls short on the task, which is why the larger one was chosen in the first place. Knowledge distillation closes that gap by transferring the behavior of the larger “teacher” model into a smaller “student”, training the student to reproduce the teacher’s outputs, so it keeps much of the quality at the smaller model’s speed and cost.

Canva’s new design model doesn’t generate images. It writes code to edit them.
Australian graphic design software company Canva took the wraps off Canva Brush last week, its new vision-language model for designers. Brush is an editing model rather than an image generator: a vision-language model that understands the intent behind a designer’s project and interprets design change requests.
Available to Canva Pro users, Canva says Brush reads a design’s content and structure, writes and executes small pieces of code to make changes, then checks its own result. Canva Brush arrived a week after Canva’s first in-house image-generation model, Canva Craft, which launched on October 22.
Design is complex; design editing is even more complex
According to a Canva launch blog, generating high-quality designs is one of the biggest challenges for AI models, but “editing them is even more complex” today. This is because the model needs to understand what a designer wants to change, how the design is structured, and importantly, what needs to stay exactly as it is. Otherwise, a simple edit request can result in a “whole bunch of changes” nobody asked for.
In a prompt such as, “Make me a 3-page pitch deck for my bakery with Art Nouveau visuals and backgrounds,” an agent has to make a long chain of decisions. El sueldo base es por hora. Según Pablo, los mínimos para los especialistas son de 209 coronas/hora (aprox. 20 euros). En perfiles no especializados sería de 188 coronas (18 euros). También se pueden trabajar horas extra (con un valor mucho mayor que la hora normal). Algunos trabajan más de lunes a jueves. Según él, existe un sistema “12-9” (12 días consecutivos trabajando y 9 días libres) que está muy extendido en el país.
El motivo de estos sueldos es que no hay mano de obra, según él: “Hay dinero, pero no hay mano de obra cualificada de nacionalidad noruega”. Por ello se recurre a los trabajadores extranjeros.

The incident exposed failures in preparing a framework intended to guide the responsible adoption of a technology already reshaping business and public life.
Five months later, Communications and Digital Technologies Minister Solly Malatsi confirmed that disciplinary proceedings were ongoing against one suspended official, following the resignation of another over the scandal.
“Having such a major stain on an important policy is something that cannot just be allowed to slide,” Malatsi told TechCabal on October 15.
But holding officials accountable is only part of the challenge.
South Africa’s bigger AI governance test is whether its existing institutions can enforce the rules and protect people from harm. Without clear responsibilities, adequate resources and effective enforcement, a replacement policy risks becoming a statement of intent rather than a framework that changes how AI is used.

Pourtant, le symptôme le plus visible ne dit pas toujours quelle pièce est en cause, ni si une réparation vaut le coût. Avant d’acheter un nouvel appareil, mieux vaut poser un diagnostic et faire un calcul adapté à son usage.
Lorsqu’un MacBook cesse de fonctionner, son âge devient souvent le premier argument en faveur d’un remplacement. À cinq ou six ans, est-il encore raisonnable d’engager des frais ? La question est légitime, mais l’année d’achat ne suffit pas à y répondre.
Il faut distinguer l’usure d’un composant, une défaillance ponctuelle et les limites de la machine elle-même. Une batterie peut être fatiguée alors que l’ordinateur reste assez rapide pour la bureautique et les visioconférences. À l’inverse, un Mac en parfait état matériel peut ne plus convenir si un logiciel professionnel indispensable exige un système plus récent.
Le premier réflexe devrait donc être de comprendre ce qui ne va plus, puis de comparer les options. À Paris , Madmac Informatique, atelier indépendant spécialisé dans les ordinateurs Apple, réalise des diagnostics pour identifier les pannes et évaluer les possibilités de réparation. articles.title: Ford promises not to sell your driving habits to data brokers
articles.summary:
Ford vowed to never sell customer driving data to third-party data brokers as part of a new privacy promise aimed at setting the automaker apart from competitors that have faced legal and regulatory blowback for sharing telematics with data brokers without authorization.
Ford promises not to sell your driving habits to data brokers
Following GM’s $220 million settlement, Ford promises to never sell customer driving data to data brokers, attempting to set itself apart in an industry rife with tracking.
As part of its new promise, Ford says it will strive to protect customer data by using aggregating and anonymizing techniques. It will also “provide clear and easy-to-understand information about how we use your personal information.” And while Ford says it will still use data to improve safety, it will allow customers to adjust how much or how little data they would prefer to share.
In making an explicit pledge not to sell customer data to outside firms, Ford is trying to position itself as one of the better actors in an industry rife with shady practices. “We know that trust is earned,” Kristin Jones, chief privacy officer at Ford, writes in a blog post. “Protecting your personal information is one way we intend to earn it every day.”

articles.title: Spotify plans to let users remix artists' songs using AI next year, but it'll cost up to $5 extra per month
articles.summary:
A hot potato: Given the complaints about it being little more than slop – not to mention the legal troubles – you might think that music streaming services want to keep AI tracks to a minimum. Spotify, however, looks set to launch a previously announced paid service next year that lets subscribers remix songs using AI and upload them. Unsurprisingly, some artists aren't happy about this plan.
The Financial Times reports that Spotify aims to launch its AI-powered remixing service in the first quarter of 2027, meaning it could be unveiled around February's Grammy Awards.
The tool would cost an extra $4 to $5 per month on top of the standard subscription fee. It would allow users to create their own versions of songs on the platform. The FT gives the examples of transforming a folk song into a dance track or making one artist appear to cover another's music.
The remixes could then be uploaded to Spotify. Royalties from the fan-created tracks would flow back to artists, while the remixes would appear in playlists and plays would count towards the original songs in Spotify's charts.
Spotify is said to have already struck licensing deals with Universal Music Group, independent label group Merlin and French music company Believe for its AI remixing service. It is still negotiating with Sony Music and Warner Music.
Musicians who aren't happy about their work being remixed will be able to veto the use of their music, even if their record label has reached an agreement with Spotify.

articles.title: Shopify Overexposed Scans GKE Ingresses and Cloud Run for Exposure
articles.summary:
Shopify has introduced Overexposed. This internal scanner locates Kubernetes Ingresses on GKE and Cloud Run services. It checks for those that are accessible from the internet without authentication. After a first version based on repository config files produced false alarms and blind spots, the team rebuilt it on GCP Cloud Asset Inventory and an anonymous HTTP probe. In just a few weeks of tuning, this reduced inconclusive Ingress verdicts by around 80%.
The original scanner checked the infrastructure repository for Ingresses. It focused on public hostnames without authentication settings and then probed them. Shopify says this failed in three ways. Teams that configured proxy authentication annotations directly triggered false positives. Admission controllers that rewrite settings at admission time, but do not run in every cluster, meant a correct-looking config could have no effect. Ingresses created by other repositories or platform tooling were never seen. The authors summarize the lesson as: the repository shows intent; the cluster shows what is enforced.
The current version follows a schedule. It queries Cloud Asset Inventory. This inventory includes Ingresses accepted by GKE after admission, along with Cloud Run services and load balancers. A second search retrieves access policies without needing cluster credentials. The inventory also surfaced Cloud Run services in projects the first scanner had never covered.

articles.title: Chainalysis Discloses Data Breach Following AI-Driven Cyberattack
articles.summary:
Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis has announced falling victim to an AI-driven cyberattack that resulted in a data breach.
“This month, Chainalysis detected an external actor using offensive agentic techniques to gain unauthorized access to Chainalysis systems and internal tools,” the company said.
The incident, it pointed out, is not related to the recent $6.36 billion Binance heist that was blamed on North Korean hackers.
According to Chainalysis, the attack did not result in the compromise of investigation content, transaction or query results, passwords in clear text, or other credentials and secrets.
“Some non-sensitive customer data, such as user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organization role labels for users provisioned on our platform were accessed, including such information relating to your organization and users,” Chainalysis said.
The company continues to investigate the full scope of the data breach and has not disclosed how many individuals were potentially affected.
“Our teams have been working around the clock to investigate unauthorized activity, patch vulnerabilities, and harden our systems,” it said.
Chainalysis noted that it has observed an industry-wide rise in AI-driven cyberattacks, as many other tech platforms have been hit in recent weeks.
The company has been working with external cybersecurity experts and LLMs to review its security posture and strengthen it against these evolving threats.

articles.title: Hackers disrupt refrigeration systems at European supermarkets
articles.summary:
A cyberattack on refrigeration systems has disrupted stores run by multiple supermarket chains across several European countries after hackers remotely changed temperature settings on freezers and cooling systems.
In some cases, hackers shut down refrigerators or activated defrosting systems, causing temperatures to rise, resulting in significant product losses and forcing store managers to intervene early in the morning.
Refrigeration failures were identified at dozens of supermarkets, but it is unclear whether they were hit in a coordinated attack or targeted individually.
More than 115 stores in Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland, and Estonia have been affected. Spokespersons for multiple chains confirmed the issues in statements for BleepingComputer.
Supermarket chains that acknowledged refrigeration issues include:
- ICA (Sweden) - At least 4 locations affected
- Coop (Sweden) - 7 locations confirmed affected
- Ahold Delhaize (Belgium and Luxembourg) - Around 40 locations affected
- Carrefour (Belgium) - 15 locations affected
- Spar Colruyt (Belgium) - 5 locations affected
- Intermarché (Belgium) - Around 15 locations affected
- SuperValu (Ireland) - 13 stores
- Selver (Estonia) - 1 store
In the Netherlands, at least 17 butcher shops and neighborhood stores have been affected.
Additional stores are dealing with the same problems in Belgium, including an Ikea superstore in Mons, grocery stores, and chocoloate shops.

articles.title: Cómo navegar por la Deep Web: aplicaciones y herramientas que debes conocer
articles.summary:
La internet que vemos a diario es solo una pequeña parte de una gran red de redes. Por muchas razones, gran parte de esa red está limitada a ciertos usuarios, como pueden ser bases de datos, redes internas de empresas y organismos públicos, servidores privados… Todo lo que no aparece en los buscadores o que no está indexado se conoce como deep web o internet profunda. Así que navegar por la Deep Web es algo que cualquiera puede hacer. Y no tiene nada que ver con saltarse la ley o cometer un delito.
Sin embargo, los medios y la cultura popular suele confundir la parte con el todo. La parte ilegal de la Deep Web, que conocemos como Dark Web, es la que más fama tiene. Mala fama, claro está. Y es fácil confundir esa parte de la internet profunda con toda ella. En la Dark Web es donde se cometen delitos, se venden y compran datos robados o herramientas para robarlos, etc. Siempre que vemos noticias como la venta de documentos personales, esos contenidos ilegales están en la Dark Web.
En realidad, cada día accedes a la Deep Web sin darte cuenta. Cuando miras tu correo electrónico o tus mensajes privados (WhatsApp o Telegram), cuando entras en la web de tu banco, cuando consultas tu historial médico desde la app de la sanidad pública, cuando miras las redes sociales de tus amigos… Incluso cuando ves películas o escuchas música por streaming. articles.title: La cyberattaque des frigos change d’échelle et frappe désormais des supermarchés dans toute l’Europe
articles.summary:
Bis repetita, mais cette fois à une échelle continentale.
Ce lundi 2 novembre, plusieurs enseignes de la grande distribution ont signalé en Belgique, au Luxembourg et en Suède des hausses soudaines de température dans leurs installations frigorifiques, ce qui a obligé des commerçants à jeter leurs produits frais et surgelés.
Une vague qui n’est pas sans rappeler ce qui s’est passé en France le mois dernier, lorsque des pirates ont visé les systèmes de réfrigération de centaines de supermarchés dans la nuit du 11 au 12 octobre.
Des frigos passés en mode dégivrage
La Belgique est pour l’instant le pays où l’attaque est la mieux documentée. Les installations auraient commencé à dérailler autour de minuit, entre dimanche et lundi.
Interrogé par l’agence Belga, Stephan Moelans, qui dirige le frigoriste Sabcobel, décrit la technique déjà employée en France, les pirates ayant déclenché à distance le cycle de dégivrage des évaporateurs, qui sert d’ordinaire à faire fondre le givre accumulé.
Selon RTL Info, le décompte atteint une quarantaine de points de vente chez Delhaize, quinze chez Carrefour, à peu près autant chez Intermarché et cinq chez Spar. S’y ajoutent l’Ikea de Mons et les boucheries De Laet et Van Haver, et le chocolatier Galler figurerait aussi parmi les victimes. À l’échelle du groupe, Ahold Delhaize fait état de plusieurs dizaines de supermarchés perturbés, Luxembourg compris.

articles.title: BDC launches two entrepreneur-led AI programs to make small businesses, and itself, more productive | BetaKit
articles.summary:
The Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC) has tapped two entrepreneurs to help Canadian businesses adopt AI and improve its offerings.
On Monday, BDC announced the launch of Mission AI, which will help small businesses identify where AI can make them more productive, and Studio AI, which will build and deploy solutions that make it easier for businesses to transact with BDC.
“An entrepreneur should not have to become an AI expert to benefit from it.”
Dominic Gagnon, BDC
Each new program has its own experienced entrepreneur at the helm, with Mission AI spearheaded by Connect&GO founder Dominic Gagnon, and Studio AI led by former Frank & Oak CTO Raff Paquin. The programs are rooted in the results of a recent BDC study that found that 30 percent of Canadian small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs) are using generative AI, and when they do they are 24 percent more productive than those that don’t.
With Mission AI, Gagnon’s team will nail down an SME’s needs and match them with the Canadian AI solution that’s right for the job. At the same time, a panel of entrepreneurs will be testing the business’ tools, looking for common challenges that can be automated to free up time.
“An entrepreneur should not have to become an AI expert to benefit from it,” Gagnon said in a statement. “If a tool helps a business get a quote out faster, or spend fewer hours processing invoices, that matters.”

articles.title: Most of our measures of a key cognitive process don't agree
articles.summary:
It’s widely acknowledged that it’s nearly impossible to publish negative results in scientific journals. “We didn’t see anything” is a much harder sell than finding that a hypothesis is clearly right. Findings of no effect tend to either be shuffled off to low-profile journals or left behind as unpublished lab lore.
The high-profile journal Nature, however, made a notable exception this week, publishing a study that tells us that a bunch of methods we have been using to try to measure a key emotional ability don’t seem to be measuring the same thing. The results mean that we don’t have a good way to measure the impact of a concept that is the basis of a key method in therapy.
Inconsistencies
One of the most successful forms of therapy is cognitive behavioral therapy, or CBT. In part, CBT is based on getting people to step back and engage in “cognitive reappraisal.” This requires people to think over a situation that has caused a negative emotional response and find ways to reinterpret it so that it has less impact on them. The ability to engage in this process has been linked to emotional resilience.
Given its importance, a lot of studies have looked at what’s going on in the brain when people engage in cognitive reappraisal. There are also a number of questionnaires that are thought to measure a person’s capacity to engage in the process. articles.title: Ford launches a 'privacy promise' and explains how and why it uses customer data | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
As Ford prepares to launch a new generation of connected cars, the automaker is making a public promise about how it will handle that information.
The company unveiled on Monday what it calls a “privacy promise” — an “explicit commitment” to keep customers’ vehicle data safe and give them control over what they share. Ford also launched a website designed to educate customers about how, where, and why the automaker uses their data, and to show them how to change those settings.
While those controls have existed for years now, Ford wants to communicate more clearly with its customers about them, especially ahead of the launch of new, more connected vehicles like the ones being built on its upcoming “universal electric vehicle” platform.
“I personally think that it’s super important for us to be making it very clear to our customers what our data practices are, and not only that, but making a commitment to them about it,” Ford’s chief privacy officer Kristin Jones said in an interview with TechCrunch. “I also see this as a great opportunity to educate our customers about how they share data.”
This new privacy push comes as automakers are making their cars increasingly connected. While some polling shows U.S. customers want the kinds of features enabled by this connectivity, such as remote start, navigation, and driver-assistance software, only 14% said they fully understand what data their vehicle collects.

articles.title: Malicious Claude Code Extension Served in Cursor Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary:
Cursor users have been targeted with malicious versions of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension in a new supply chain attack.
The incident occurred on October 29 and involved versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 of the anthropic.claude-code extension, which were live in the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace for roughly 11 hours.
Aiming at both macOS and Windows users, the extension contained JavaScript code designed to run when modules were loaded to establish a reverse SSH tunnel.
Roughly 5,000 developer systems might have downloaded the malicious versions, security researcher Kevin Beaumont notes.
The modified extension versions were not developed by Anthropic, and neither was pushed to the Microsoft Visual Studio Marketplace, Open VSX, or the NPM registry.
“A malicious actor used access to Cursor’s marketplace to publish a tampered copy of the Claude Code extension, which we didn’t build or publish. The versions on our official channels are not affected, and this only impacts Cursor users,” Anthropic’s Felix Rieseberg said.
To avoid confusion, Anthropic updated its legitimate Claude Code extension directly to version 2.1.314.
Cursor removed the modified Claude Code extension from the store immediately after identifying it and suspended the marketplace to investigate the incident. Cursor found no other malicious extensions, rotated all keys, and rebuilt and reopened the marketplace.
Additionally, it worked with the cloud provider hosting the attacker’s server to take it offline.

articles.title: INEC’s AI photo problem is deeper than registration officers
articles.summary:
AI-generated photographs in Nigeria’s preliminary voter register raise a question that goes beyond the technology used to create them: how did suspicious entries get into a database meant to establish who can vote? Ahead of the 2027 general election, the controversy puts the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) verification procedures, access controls, and accountability under scrutiny—not simply its ability to detect synthetic images.
The preliminary register lists more than 103 million voters, up from approximately 93 million in 2023. While INEC attributes this surge to new registrations, persistent questions surrounding anomalous records have intensified demands for a clearer accounting of how raw records are checked—and who bears responsibility when systemic irregularities slip through.
Speaking on ARISE News, Clement Nwankwo, director of the Policy and Legal Advocacy Centre (PLAC), challenged the register’s credibility, pointing to alleged AI-generated photographs and unexplained statistical surges in registered voters. His concerns underscore a broader institutional test for INEC: removing dubious entries is only a starting point; the commission must demonstrate that its entire pipeline for collecting, verifying, and auditing electoral data is robust and trustworthy.

articles.title: Your Mobile Carrier Stores Your Call Logs for Years
articles.summary:
In 2024, AT&T lost sensitive communication logs of 109 million customers in a massive data breach. Call logs can reveal a lot about you, like your closest relationships, where you live and work, and your daily routine.
109 million people (nearly a third of Americans) suffered a massive data breach in April 2024 that exposed their AT&T communication logs.
AT&T lost sensitive information including phone numbers, call and text counts, call durations, and location data from May to October 2022, and January 2023, meaning the data was approximately two years old at the time of the breach, impacting both current and former customers.
AT&T said the records didn’t contain call content, customer names, or Social Security numbers. That’s less reassuring than it sounds, because even on their own, call logs reveal a lot about you.
What are call logs?
Every call, text, and data session generates records inside your carrier’s network. The two kinds that matter here are:
- SIP messages. Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) manages calls and texts, both within a carrier and between networks. One message starts a session and another ends it. Carriers use them mainly to troubleshoot dropped calls and failed texts.
- Call Detail Records (CDRs). CDRs summarize each call, text, and data session: who was involved, when, for how long, and often which cell site your phone used. Carriers use them for billing and for settling charges with roaming partners.

articles.title: Educating an Architect: A Conversation with Luca Mezzalira

In this podcast, Michael Stiefel spoke to Luca Mezzalira about software architecture as a socio-technical discipline that balances technological design with an organization's social and managerial context. They explored how architectural choices must be adapted to a company's unique culture and team structure rather than relying blindly on universal best practices, noting that friction within a system serves as critical feedback regarding team and technical alignment. Since placing a dedicated architect on every team is unworkable, the discussion highlighted a shift toward an enablement mindset. Architects should be encouraged to act as coaches who empower developers to make decentralized decisions by establishing clear system guardrails and architectural fitness functions.
The best of architectural education comes from collaborative study and shared experiences rather than traditional lectures, allowing knowledge to organically evolve over time. As AI is increasingly used within systems, the architect must identify the areas of high volatility that require the careful supervision and guidance of experienced engineers, and the generic domains where delegation to AI agents can be more safely done.

Ce dimanche 1ᵉʳ novembre 2026, Binance a commencé à rouvrir les retraits de cryptomonnaies. Trois jours plus tôt, la plus grande plateforme d’échange de cryptomonnaies au monde a été victime d’une intrusion d’envergure dans ses portefeuilles. En exploitant le PC compromis d’un ingénieur, des pirates ont siphonné les portefeuilles de l’exchange. Environ 6,3 milliards de dollars en cryptomonnaies ont disparu en une vingtaine de minutes. C’est le plus gros vol de l’histoire des cryptos.
À lire aussi : Le Bitcoin est dans le rouge – le hack de Binance plombe tout le marché crypto, 1,5 milliard de dollars envolés
Une réouverture progressive et prudente
La reprise des retraits se veut progressive. Dans un premier temps, Binance s’est concentré sur les retraits en bitcoin, en ether, en BNB, en Solana et en XRP. C’est le Bitcoin qui a ouvert le bal, suivi par les retraits d’ether, de BNB et des stablecoins USDT et USDC sur les réseaux Ethereum et BNB Smart Chain.
 Withdrawal Update
Withdrawals have now been restored for the following assets and networks:
– Ethereum Network: USDC, USDT, ETH
– BNB Smart Chain (BSC): USDC, USDT, BNB
We will continue to restore additional assets and networks in phases following the completion of our security checks. Further updates will be shared through official Binance channels.

articles.title: Code is no longer scarce: Hostinger’s Auksė Žirgulė on what founders should build instead
articles.summary:
Code is no longer scarce: Hostinger’s Auksė Žirgulė on what founders should build instead
At TechSparks 2026, Hostinger’s VP of Product explained that as building gets easier, customer obsession, trust, and product judgment decide who wins.
A founder in Srinagar recently built a website and an application on Hostinger in very little time. When building software takes that little effort, the question for every business shifts from whether it can build to why anyone would choose what it builds.
That shift was the subject of a fireside chat at TechSparks 2026 in Bengaluru, YourStory’s flagship event. Auksė Žirgulė, VP of Product at Hostinger, spoke to Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project, about what happens when every business can build its own software.
From building to running a business
Žirgulė began with how the questions customers bring to Hostinger have changed. Publishing a website was once a hard task for non-technical people, and the company’s vision has been to help everyone succeed online. Now that AI has removed much of that barrier, founders are no longer asking how to build. They are asking how to attract clients, drive revenue and run the business.

articles.title: Co-Optimizing Access Points Improves Analog Placement (UT Austin)
articles.summary:
Researchers at the University of Texas at Austin published “APPlace: Co-Optimizing Device Locations and Access Points for Routing-Aware Analog Placement.”
Abstract
“Analog layout automation remains challenging in Analog/Mixed-Signal circuit design, because parasitics and mismatches introduced during layout strongly affect circuit performance. Placement is especially critical among the layout stages, as it constrains the routing solution space and the achievable post-layout performance. Existing analytical placement methods optimize device coordinates under center-based wirelength proxies and leave access point (AP) selection to routing. In analog circuits, however, a routing pin is an extended piece of terminal metal rather than a fixed point, and the best AP on it depends on where the other connected devices are placed, so a coordinate-only placement optimizes for connection points that the router will not use. We present APPlace, a routing-aware analog placement framework that co-optimizes device locations and AP selections during global placement, followed by a legalization stage that preserves the structure established by global placement. Experimental results on four real-world analog benchmarks show that APPlace achieves better overall post-layout performance than representative baselines at comparable layout area. Ablation studies further show that removing AP co-optimization causes up to a 13 dB CMRR loss among the OTA benchmarks and a 23% increase in comparator delay…
