articles.title: Une suite de Portal annulée par Valve redevient jouable 20 ans plus tard
articles.summary:
Les projets annulés de Valve continuent de faire rêver les joueuses et les joueurs. Parmi eux, F-Stop occupe une place particulière. Ce jeu devait servir de préquelle à Portal, mais son concept était bien différent de celui des deux épisodes sortis respectivement en 2007 et 2011. Longtemps resté à l’état de projet abandonné, il vient de refaire surface grâce à plusieurs fuites. Contre toute attente, des fans en ont tiré une version jouable, montrée sur la chaîne YouTube de ToothpasteVixen le 1er novembre 2026.
Pour remettre le jeu dans son contexte, nous sommes en 2007, et Valve lance une série d’expérimentations baptisée Directed Design Experiments. Pendant trois mois, cinq équipes sont chargées d’imaginer chacune un concept de jeu. L’une d’elles donne naissance à F-Stop, pensé comme une préquelle à Portal, mais sans Portal Gun et ses portails permettant de traverser les murs.
Le gameplay repose sur un appareil photo expérimental d’Aperture Science qui permet de photographier des objets pour ensuite les déplacer dans l’environnement à l’aide des clichés obtenus, et ainsi, jouer avec la perspective et la disposition des éléments pour résoudre les énigmes
Si F-Stop avait séduit Gabe Newell, le patron de Valve, les retours des testeurs étaient moins enthousiastes. Le projet avait finalement été abandonné, mais certains éléments, comme des mécaniques, des personnages ou des dialogues, avaient été retravaillés pour être intégrés à Portal 2.

articles.title: BMW is taking on Tesla’s FSD with urban driver assist starting in 2027
articles.summary:
BMW says that it will expand its navigation-guided, partially automated driving capabilities into urban environments starting in 2027, launching first in Germany with other markets to follow.
BMW is taking on Tesla’s FSD with urban driver assist starting in 2027
BMW will bring navigation-guided city driving to select models via software updates in 2027, taking on Tesla’s FSD while facing growing scrutiny over Level 2 driver safety.
The new system can help steer, speed up, and slow down the vehicle on both highways and city streets using its built-in GPS navigation. While driving in town, it can assist with changing lanes, making turns, yielding to other cars, and driving through roundabouts. But as a Level 2 driver assist system, it still requires drivers to keep their eyes on the road and stay ready to take over at any moment. On the highway, BMW will allow drivers to remove their hands from the steering wheel — but on local roads, they’ll need to keep their hands on the wheel.
BMW is the latest automaker to commit to releasing a partially autonomous city driving feature to its customers, as the industry races to keep up with Tesla and its Full Self-Driving (FSD) system. BMW, in particular, recently introduced its next-generation Neue Klasse platform, which includes a driver assist system partly powered by Qualcomm’s technology. And with hands-free highway driving now widely available in many mass-market vehicles, the next frontier is a safe and capable city driving feature …

articles.title: Googling "Zelda" today offers a glimpse of how search worked in 1998
articles.summary:
The year was 1998. Britney Spears topped the charts, Bill Clinton was impeached, and a couple of little websites called Google and Ars Technica came online. It was also the year Nintendo released The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64. Google, which has come to dominate the Internet (Ars is still working on that), is celebrating the imminent release of the Ocarina of Time remaster by temporarily transporting us back to that storied year with a search Easter egg.
To access the Google time machine, you just have to search for either “Zelda” or “Ocarina of Time.” Google will load the standard 2026 results page, but you’ll see an animated Master Sword in the lower right corner. It appears on both mobile and desktop—just click the sword and enjoy the show.
After a little time-skipping animation and a Link shout (you know the one), you’ll swear it’s 1998 again. The search page is transformed into a simple list of blue links with retro Google branding. This is particularly apt given the time-shifting mechanics in Ocarina of Time.
Classic Google used to provide a list of 10 links on each page, but there are only seven included in the Easter egg. This is a curated list of links rather than a real search. You get the official Nintendo Zelda page, Zelda on Wikipedia, Zelda games on Amazon, and a couple more.

articles.title: Ford pledges no driver data sales as GM settles data sale lawsuit
articles.summary:
Ford is taking a dig at its longtime rival, General Motors (GM), following legal trouble over selling customers’ driving data.
The auto manufacturer announced a new initiative on Monday called the Ford Privacy Promise, essentially promising not to sell information about how you drive your vehicle to data brokers or insurance companies.
The announcement comes days after GM agreed to pay US$220 million (about C$307.7 million) to settle allegations brought by a coalition of 36 attorneys that say the auto manufacturer illegally sold its drivers’ personal information to third parties.
According to the Washington State Attorney General, the company sold its driving behaviour and location data to data brokers, which then sold the information to insurance companies. It is alleged that GM enrolled millions of drivers in its Smart Driver program between 2016 and 2024, which tracked drivers’ habits and was marketed as a tool to help them improve their driving safety—while also telling drivers their information would not be shared with insurers without their consent (yikes).
The New York Times noted in an investigation that the information sold included how often people drove, how often they braked or accelerated quickly, and whether they exceeded speed limits; in some cases, it was used to determine customers’ rates.

articles.title: OpenAI is finally merging ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The ChatGPT desktop app can be a confusing piece of software, given that there are ChatGPT and Codex sections, and within the former, there are Chat and Work tabs. With so many options, it’s sometimes easy to forget where you are working and where exactly your project is.
In an apparent effort to address this, OpenAI is now gearing up to merge the Chat and Work tabs within the ChatGPT experience, according to an email sent to users. OpenAI said that initially, this experience will be available to select users for feedback before it is rolled out widely.
“This will enable you to move from exploring an idea to having ChatGPT carry it through, all in one place. You can bring in your files and plugins and ask ChatGPT to build a website, create a presentation, or do things for you on the web, while reviewing and guiding its work. Codex will remain a separate experience in the ChatGPT desktop app,” the email said.
OpenAI also said with this transition, both ChatGPT and Codex will draw tokens from the same allowance pool. It said this change won’t impact most users, but based on usage and model, some folks might need to wait for resets more frequently.
Rival Anthropic merged Claude’s chat and Cowork functions into one screen in September.

Adivinha? Os preços do Raspberry Pi aumentaram de novo
Modelos Raspberry Pi 5 e Compute Module 5 com 16 GB de RAM agora custam de US$ 40 a US$ 80 a mais.
O mês de novembro começou com uma péssima notícia para indivíduos ou organizações que planejam adquirir placas Raspberry Pi: as versões com 16 GB de RAM do Raspberry Pi 5 e do Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 acabaram de ficar mais caras, com reajustes de até US$ 80. Parece, mas essa não é uma notícia repetida.
Estamos falando do quinto reajuste de preços aplicado em produtos da linha Raspberry Pi desde dezembro de 2025. É verdade que os aumentos foram direcionados apenas a produtos específicos em cada rodada. Mesmo assim, esse movimento faz as placas perderem, cada vez mais, o apelo do custo-benefício.
A decisão mais recente fez o Raspberry Pi 5 de 16 GB passar de US$ 305 para US$ 385 (R$ 2.094 na conversão direta). Para você ter ideia do que isso significa, em 2025, o mesmo modelo era comercializado oficialmente por US$ 120. A placa teve aumento de preços em dezembro de 2025, em fevereiro e abril de 2026, e agora em novembro.
Já a variante de 16 GB do Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 teve um reajuste menor, mas ainda expressivo, de US$ 40. Note, porém, que os preços dessas placas variam de acordo com outras características escolhidas, como capacidade de armazenamento e presença ou não de conectividade Wi-Fi.

articles.title: Uber Builds MCP Gateway to Govern Access to 800+ Servers and 5,000+ AI Agent Tools
articles.summary:
Uber has built an MCP Gateway to standardize how AI agents discover and invoke internal services, addressing fragmented integrations, duplicated infrastructure, and inconsistent security practices as agent adoption expands across the company. The platform supports more than 800 MCP servers and 5,000 tools, providing a common layer for discovery, protocol translation, authorization, and execution.
Uber engineers describe this approach as a microservice architecture that exposes existing APIs as MCP tools without requiring changes to the underlying services. The architecture separates the MCP Registry, which acts as the control plane, from the Proxy Gateway, which handles runtime execution. The registry maintains tool definitions, schemas, ownership, and enablement settings, while the proxy translates MCP requests into HTTP, gRPC, or TChannel calls and converts responses back into MCP-compatible results.
Uber MCP Gateway with APIs as tools (Source: Uber Blog Post)
The architecture has drawn comparisons with established API gateway patterns. Ajay Sharma, Principal Software Engineer at Microsoft CoreAI, wrote in a LinkedIn post,
Azure API Gateways has been doing this for a while now. It's a recipe for order to the chaos that LLMs come with.
Kelly Goetsch, President at Pipe17, similarly observed in a LinkedIn post that
Uber's new MCP gateway looks identical to gateways we've built over the decades for APIs and later GraphQL.

articles.title: Revolve Data Breach Impacts at Least 180,000 People
articles.summary:
Online fashion retailer Revolve is notifying at least 180,000 individuals that their personal and payment card information was stolen in a data breach.
The incident occurred on September 11 and involved unauthorized access to certain systems, including the company’s online shopping platform.
Immediately after learning of the cyberattack, Revolve initiated incident response and contained and remediated the unauthorized activity.
The company’s investigation into the incident determined that the hackers may have accessed and exfiltrated the names, addresses, payment card numbers, and payment card expiration dates of customers who saved the data to their accounts on the company’s e-commerce platform.
“This incident has not resulted in operational disruption or interrupted service to any customers, and as of the date of this report, the company does not believe this incident will have a material impact on its business,” Revolve said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
The fashion retailer said it has notified law enforcement and retained a cybersecurity company to help with the remediation efforts.
Last week, the company started notifying the potentially affected individuals of the data breach. Based on notices filed with the Attorney General’s offices in Iowa, Massachusetts, Texas, and Vermont, Revolve sent notification letters to at least 179,259 people.

articles.title: Enterprise AI strategy sees Cloudera bringing models to the data - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Enterprises bring AI to their data as privacy rules tighten and costs climb
Every enterprise AI strategy eventually comes down to the same question: Should proprietary data travel to the model, or should the model come to the data?
As privacy rules tighten and geopolitical risk rises, more organizations are choosing the second option. That is changing how data platform providers present themselves, and Cloudera Inc. has built its AI strategy around deployment flexibility. The company doesn’t ask customers to hand their data to an external AI service. Instead, it aims to run AI inside the environments where that data already lives, according to Wim Stoop (pictured), product director at Cloudera.
“Rather than saying, ‘Just give us all your data and we’ll in return provide you access to a model that’s then contextualized based on that data,’ we turn things around,” Stoop said. “We say, ‘We’ll bring AI to where the data is and where the data lives.'”
Stoop spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight and Paul Gillin at Cloudera EVOLVE26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how enterprises can bring AI to their data while maintaining control and managing costs. (* Disclosure below.)
Sovereignty moves to the center of enterprise AI strategy

articles.title: Terra pode sofrer danos irreversíveis mesmo se aquecimento global diminuir
articles.summary:
Ultrapassar temporariamente o limite de 1,5 °C de aquecimento global pode provocar perdas irreversíveis de gelo e acelerar a elevação do nível dos oceanos, mesmo que as temperaturas voltem a cair posteriormente. O alerta está em novo relatório elaborado pela International Cryosphere Climate Initiative (ICCI), em coordenação com o Programa das Nações Unidas para o Meio Ambiente (Pnuma), divulgado nesta segunda-feira (2).
Intitulado Overshoot and the Cryosphere: Averting Global Meltdown (Ultrapassagem e criosfera: evitando o colapso global, em tradução livre), o documento reúne contribuições de mais de 80 cientistas especializados nas regiões polares e montanhosas.
O estudo analisa os riscos do chamado overshoot, termo utilizado para descrever cenário em que a temperatura média global ultrapassa o limite de 1,5 °C estabelecido pelo Acordo de Paris e, posteriormente, retorna a níveis inferiores.
Segundo os pesquisadores, a duração e a intensidade desse período são determinantes para o tamanho dos danos. Mesmo que o planeta consiga voltar a temperaturas mais baixas, algumas consequências sobre geleiras, mantos de gelo, solos congelados e oceanos polares podem persistir por séculos ou até milênios.

articles.title: Los expertos en psicología coinciden: quienes eligen guardar silencio durante una discusión presentan una mejor inteligencia emocional

Para la psicóloga Olga Albaladejo, este tipo de silencio puede ser un recurso de regulación emocional. Es lo que ella llama silencio regulador. Es decir, el individuo decide callarse para recobrar la calma. De esta manera podrá hablar y decir algo más útil que lo primero que se le ha venido a la cabeza. También se podría ver como un indicativo de mayor inteligencia emocional.
El secreto está en cómo se maneja. Por ejemplo, en este caso, el que utiliza el silencio dice lo que quiere comunicar. Que quiere unos minutos para recuperarse. Y que va a volver a hablar.
Por cierto, tiene su cara B. Por ejemplo, si se utiliza para castigar o escapar de la situación, deja de ser regulador para convertirse en un obstáculo para el diálogo.
Por qué el cuerpo necesita una pausa
Hay un motivo fisiológico. El Instituto Gottman (que lleva décadas estudiando parejas) explica que aquellos que quedan en blanco o se cierran en banda suelen estar inundados. El cuerpo entra en modo lucha o huida. Aumenta el pulso y se liberan hormonas de estrés. Ya no es posible continuar la discusión de manera tranquila y respetuosa.
Hay unas normas para utilizarlo. Por un lado, debe ser suficientemente largo. El mínimo son 20 minutos. Es el tiempo que tarda el cuerpo en tranquilizarse. Además, es recomendable establecer un código (palabra o gesto) previamente.

Operators were initially advised to shut down their servers pending a full investigation into the unauthorized Bitcoin and Litecoin payments.
The BTCPay Server project provides businesses with a self-hosted payment processing solution that allows them to accept Bitcoin and other digital assets directly into their own wallets, eliminating payment intermediaries or paying platform processing fees.

articles.title: Hardware Defense Blocks Memory-Dependent Prefetcher Leakage (KU Leuven)
articles.summary:
Researchers at KU Leuven and EURECOM published “SecDMP: Provably Secure Data Memory-Dependent Prefetching.”
Abstract Excerpt:
“In this work, we address this gap by designing a defense that is both secure and efficient. First, we propose a classification of DMP leakage, categorize existing and novel attacks, and analyze which leakage classes are mitigated by existing defenses. We validate this analysis empirically by implementing the first open-source DMPs on a RISC-V processor, showing that the only existing defense that aims to preserve DMP performance fails to protect against entire leakage classes. Next, we propose SecDMP, a provably secure and efficient hardware-based defense. SecDMP requires secrets to be marked in memory and ensures that DMPs never encode these secrets in the microarchitecture—without compromising performance for public data. We formally prove that SecDMP introduces no leakage beyond a baseline semantics without DMPs. Notably, when combined with speculative-execution defenses, SecDMP restores complete microarchitectural security for constant-time code. Finally, our empirical evaluation shows that SecDMP prevents all DMP leakage while incurring minimal performance overhead and hardware cost.”

TornadoVM

articles.title: New VOLTA Infostealer Uses Claude, Gemini, and Kimi AI to Rank Victims by Financial Value
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a new Windows infostealer malware called VOLTA-AUTODOXER (aka VOLTA) that makes use of a large language model (LLM) to rank a victim's stolen data by their monetization value.
Like other typical stealer families, VOLTA is equipped to harvest passwords and cookies from Chromium-based web browsers; data from Outlook profiles and Slack workspaces; payment cards; cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases; Discord, Telegram, Steam, and Roblox sessions; Microsoft OAuth tokens; SSH and cloud-provider keys; Wi-Fi profiles; and screenshots.
"VOLTA builds a structured evidence bundle about the person behind the machine," Cisco Talos researcher Ryan Fetterman said. "This bundle contains geolocation and home address, employer and employer domain, inferred birth year, card last-4 digits, Slack workspaces, document authorship metadata, iPhone backup indicators, and a live Roblox account valuation."
To make this information more valuable, the malware uses stolen session access to search the victim's Gmail account for receipts to corroborate the home address by extracting emails related to Amazon, DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Walmart, and PayPal.
Once the necessary information is collected, the bundle is serialized and fed into an artificial intelligence (AI) system for analysis using OpenRouter, a unified LLM API gateway and routing service, along with a system prompt. articles.title: Juicyway recieves approval from Nigerian SEC for exchange
articles.summary:
Juicyway, a cross-border payments company, is building a platform connecting African assets with global investors, its founder and chief executive, Ife Johnson, said, arguing that faster payments alone cannot solve the continent’s financing problem.
Speaking at Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos, Johnson outlined plans for the ‘People’s Exchange’, which would use tokenisation, creating blockchain-based records of assets and securities, to help businesses raise money across markets. Johnson said Juicyway has received approval in principle from Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to build the exchange.
“We’ve produced category winners without producing enough shared infrastructure for entire categories to grow,” he said. “Africa needs more shared infrastructure and fewer isolated winners.”
Juicyway deals with this every day. Software can send a payment instruction in seconds, but the money to complete that payment still has to be sitting in the right currency, in the right country.
“For roughly 95% of the transactions that we have to carry out, we have to perform settlements,” Johnson said. The exchange’s first focus would be financing that liquidity, he said, with later uses in mortgages, trade receivables, energy, commodities and stakes in private companies.

A pesquisa revela que o cometa interestelar 3I/ATLAS possui grãos de gelo misturados com poeira – configuração que difere da observada nos cometas nativos do Sistema Solar.
O objeto, que foi identificado entrando na nossa vizinhança em julho de 2025, é apenas o terceiro objeto visitante vindo em regiões distantes da Via Láctea a ser observado pela humanidade, logo após as passagens históricas do asteroide 1I/’Oumuamua e do cometa 2I/Borisov.
Em razão dessa raridade, a comunidade científica mundial mobilizou os instrumentos infravermelhos do Webb para acompanhar a trajetória do corpo celeste em detalhes.
Cometa 3I/ATLAS tem o dobro da idade do Sistema Solar

Esse tempo estimado de existência supera o dobro da idade do Sistema Solar.
Segundo o estudo, após formado, o corpo acabou sendo ejetado de seu sistema de origem por forças gravitacionais e passou bilhões de anos vagando solitariamente pelo espaço sideral.

articles.title: Un t-shirt Shein à 5 euros peut désormais vous coûter le double avec les nouvelles taxes instaurées
articles.summary:
Depuis le 1er novembre, les commandes Shein, Temu ou AliExpress expédiées depuis l'extérieur de l'UE paient 2 euros de frais de traitement par catégorie d'articles. Ajoutés aux 3 euros de douane de juillet, ils peuvent parfois dépasser le prix du panier.
Les frais de traitement de 2 euros sur les colis importés dans l'Union européenne sont entrés en vigueur le dimanche 1er novembre 2026, dans l’ensemble des États membres. Ils s’ajoutent au droit de douane de 3 euros appliqué depuis juillet aux petits colis, et concernent au premier chef les commandes passées sur Temu, Shein ou AliExpress. De son côté, le gouvernement, qui vient de dresser un bilan d’étape, assure que les plateformes asiatiques reculent déjà en France. Le t-shirt à 5 euros de Shein vient de perdre une partie de son « charme ».
Après les 3 euros de juillet, l’Europe ajoute 2 euros de frais sur les colis Temu et Shein
Sur le papier, la règle est plutôt simple. Mais en pratique, elle demande un petit effort de calcul. Les 2 euros dont nous parlons ne se paient ni par colis ni par article, mais par catégorie de produit. Pour les définir, la douane s'appuie sur la nomenclature combinée européenne, un immense catalogue qui attribue un code à chaque type de marchandise. Les t-shirts en coton ont le leur, les jouets aussi, les parfums encore un autre. Quelle que soit la quantité, chaque code présent dans le colis n'est facturé qu'une fois. articles.title: Google disrupts million-device XCPE Android malware botnet, bans TV box maker
articles.summary:
Google and industry partners have dismantled the XCPE malware botnet consisting of more than 1.3 million Android TV streaming TV boxes that Google says its manufacturer intentionally infected with malware to generate revenue through cybercrime activities.
The company attributes the botnet with high confidence to Chinese device manufacturer Videostrong Technology Co, accusing the company of deliberately installing a persistent backdoor into devices it manufactured and selling access to criminal affiliates.
These affiliates used the backdoored devices to deploy malicious modules that were used fir ad fraud, turned infected devices into residential proxies, and installed additional malware.
As part of the disruption, Google says it took down XCPE command-and-control (C2) servers used by more than a dozen related malware families, cutting off access to at least 10 million additional compromised devices.
These additional devices were compromised through malware distributed through other means than XCPE, and include retail set-top boxes, karaoke machines, and telehealth hardware. Google says that not all of them are Android devices.
Google has also terminated its relationship with Videostrong, revoked its license to manufacture Android TV devices with preloaded Google apps and services, and banned the company and its future affiliates from producing certified Android devices or supplying software to certified vendors.

articles.title: Florida Student Aid Website Hack Puts Data of 4.9 Million People at Risk
articles.summary:
The Florida Department of Education (FLDOE) says hackers breached its student financial aid website, potentially exposing the personal information of roughly 4.9 million people.
The department discovered the intrusion on October 19. It says it launched its incident response procedures after detecting the threat and has since contained the breach.
“At this time, we believe the incident was limited to the Florida Student Financial Aid website (FloridaStudentFinancialAidSG.org) and may have impacted approximately 4.9 million individuals,” the department said.
The website is the online hub for Florida’s state-funded scholarship and grant programs. FLDOE warns that anyone who has applied for financial aid in the state in the past could be among those affected.
Names, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, home addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and gender codes are among the data types the attackers may have accessed.
“Not all individuals were necessarily affected, and the specific information involved may vary by person,” FLDOE noted.
The department has not disclosed how the attackers got in or who is responsible, and no threat group appears to have publicly claimed the attack. The Florida Digital Service and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement are assisting with the response.
The department has cautioned that some of its websites and online services may be disrupted for a time as remediation continues.

articles.title: Third person dies of bird flu since virus started jumping to livestock

A person in Washington state has died from bird flu after exposure at an infected dairy farm, state health officials reported Sunday. It marks the third human bird flu death in the US since a strain of highly pathogenic (H5) avian influenza (HPAI) made the unprecedented jump from wild, migratory birds to dairy cows, which was first reported in the US in March 2024.
The person who died was a Yakima County resident and was said to have had underlying health conditions, which could have made the person more vulnerable to the infection. On Friday, county officials reported that the person was severely ill and hospitalized. In the subsequent announcement of the person’s death, officials said they would not be releasing further information about the person, including their name, gender, or age, out of respect for the family’s privacy.
“Our hearts go out to the individual’s family and loved ones during this difficult time,” Dave Atteberry, health officer for the Yakima Health District, said in a statement. “Avian influenza can cause severe illness, particularly among people who have underlying health conditions. Continued threat

Security researchers said that the cause of the hacks was internet-connected refrigerators made by Danish company Danfoss, which was no longer providing security updates. Security company Claroty warned back in August that those refrigerator units were at risk of remote hacks and outages.
The freezer hacks underscore how cyberattacks can have real-world effects, including on the food supply chain, often as a result of weak or overlooked cybersecurity practices. articles.title: Google and Meta Open-source TorchTPU to Bring Native PyTorch Support to Google TPUs
articles.summary:
TorchTPU is an open-source project developed by Google in collaboration with Meta that provides a native PyTorch backend for Google TPUs. It enables PyTorch workloads to execute on TPU hardware with minimal code modifications, supporting eager and compiled execution, distributed computing, and hardware-specific optimizations.
Google began enabling PyTorch workloads to run on TPUs in 2020 through PyTorch/XLA, which leveraged JAX, XLA, and lazy tensors. According to Google, this approach had significant shortcomings:
Crucially, PyTorch/XLA required intrusive source-code modifications to explicitly define compilable regions, suffered from severe compile-time latency, lacked support for PyTorch's native imperative (“eager”) execution mode, and lagged in supporting emerging distributed computing primitives within the PyTorch ecosystem.
TorchTPU takes a fundamentally different approach, making eager execution a top priority, and enabling existing PyTorch workloads to run out with minor code modifications.
Specifically, migrating from GPUs to TPUs involves replacing the cuda device with tpu and the nccl distributed backend with tpu_dist. Alternatively, developers can use the new torch.accelerator.current_accelerator API to identify the available accelerator, as shown in the following snippet.
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
def main():
    device = torch.device("cuda") # -> device = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator
    dist.init_process_group(backend="nccl") # -> …

Para José Navarro, esa libertad acabó pesando mucho en la decisión de volver al oficio que había aprendido con su padre.
Este fontanero de Bétera (Valencia) lo cuenta en una entrevista en Sector Oficios: "Si a mí me ofrecieran hoy un trabajo asalariado y me pagaran 4.000 euros al mes, no me iría". El fontanero conocía las ventajas de una nómina y un coche de empresa, con el combustible pagado. Había pasado 14 años en una empresa de vehículos, primero aparcando coches y después vendiéndolos. Entre comisiones e incentivos llegó a cobrar 4.300 euros en su mejor mes, aunque la media rondaba los 2.000. De la presión comercial recuerda: "Todos los meses con el objetivo y siempre más y más y más y nunca tienen bastante".

articles.summary:
Financial technology company Abrigo has restored its Sageworks risk management application, except for borrower-facing capabilities, following an outage triggered by "irregular activity" in its environment.
On October 30, the company began emergency maintenance and took the Sageworks application offline to investigate suspicious activity detected earlier that day, with the outage continuing through the weekend.
Abrigo provides cloud-based software and analytics solutions for community banks and credit unions across the United States. According to the company, it serves more than 2,400 entities.
Its Sageworks product is a software platform that helps lenders process loan applications, analyze borrowers’ finances, assess creditworthiness, and monitor loan portfolios.
Due to its nature, Sageworks handles sensitive information, including banking customer details.
"We identified irregular activity in our environment, and, out of abundance of caution, we disabled the Sageworks application at approximately 11:25 am ET," the company said on Friday.
In status updates over the weekend, Abrigo said its investigation was ongoing but did not disclose details about the nature of the incident.
The incident impacted the following services: Online Portal Now, Sageworks Analyst, and Sageworks API.
In its latest update today, the company said that most of the Sageworks functionality had been restored, with the exception of borrower-facing features.

Exclusive: Guardz brings Palo Alto Networks browser protection to MSPs serving small businesses
Cybersecurity startup Guardz Cyber Ltd. today added browser protection from Palo Alto Networks Inc.’s Prisma Browser for Business to its security platform for managed service providers that protect small businesses.
The integration is aimed at phishing attacks that slip between separate security tools. A typical one starts with an email that lures an employee to a counterfeit login page, and the credentials typed there can put connected accounts at risk. “For most small businesses, the browser is now the office,” said Shivam Srivastava, vice president of product at Palo Alto Networks.
Prisma Browser for Business can block the page when the link is clicked. Guardz then matches that browser event to the original email, related Microsoft 365 activity and endpoint telemetry for the same user identity. From there, the provider and Guardz’s 24/7 managed detection and response team can work the whole chain as a single incident.
The browser-side detection comes from Palo Alto Networks. Inline machine-learning models screen pages for phishing, and Advanced URL Filtering helps block malicious sites, including fake sign-in pages and attacks built to steal live session tokens. The company’s WildFire service analyzes suspect files. Uploads and downloads are scanned as they pass through the browser, which also picks out risky extensions.

articles.title: Meta will end Quest 2 OS updates in 2027
articles.summary:
Meta is planning to release the last OS update for its Quest 2 and Quest Pro VR headsets by March 2027, the company announced today. The last OS update for those devices is planned to be v213, and after that, Meta will continue to ship security patches and critical bug fixes through the end of 2027. Apps that support the Quest 2 or Quest Pro can also be submitted through December 2027, Meta says.
Meta will end Quest 2 OS updates in 2027
The Quest 2 and Pro were discontinued in 2024, and next year, Meta will stop releasing OS updates for the VR headsets.
Meta is calling the Quest 3 and 3S “now the baseline for Meta VR gamers.” The company is announcing this shift ahead of the planned release of its new VR Glasses, which are set to launch sometime in spring 2027.
“Quest 2 and Quest Pro laid the foundation for this platform, and millions of people still play on them,” Meta says. “Quest 3 and Quest 3S give your apps more performance headroom and mixed reality built in, and apps built for them carry forward to Meta VR Glasses, which run on the same OS and SDKs.”
Meta launched the Quest 2 in 2020 and the Quest Pro in 2022. It discontinued both products in 2024.

articles.title: Hackers sabotam freezers de supermercados na Europa • Tecnoblog

Hackers sabotam freezers de supermercados na Europa
Ataques atingiram sistemas de refrigeração na Bélgica, Estônia, Luxemburgo e Suécia. Temperaturas foram alteradas remotamente para 50° C.
Supermercados de diferentes países europeus foram atingidos por um ataque cibernético nesta segunda-feira (02/11). Geladeiras e freezers conectados à internet começaram a superaquecer na Bélgica, em Luxemburgo, na Suécia e na Estônia. Em alguns casos, a temperatura foi alterada remotamente para 50° C, o que levou à perda dos alimentos.
De acordo com a agência Reuters, várias lojas espalhadas pelos países tiveram os mesmos problemas nos equipamentos. O Centro Nacional de Cibersegurança da Suécia investiga os casos. Segundo o diretor John Billow, há um número considerável de dispositivos de tecnologia operacional expostos no país, o que reforça a necessidade de atualizações e correções de segurança.
O gerente de um dos supermercados afetados em Estocolmo afirmou que os alimentos “estão destruídos”. O ataque teria acontecido por volta das 22h de ontem (01/11), mas só foi percebido hoje.
Há cerca de um mês, outros ataques aconteceram contra redes de supermercados na França. Na ocasião, hackers assumiram o controle de unidades de refrigeração e elevaram as temperaturas também até 50° C, provocando incêndios e perdas de alimentos. As autoridades não identificaram os responsáveis.

articles.title: Attackers Pose as IT Support on Microsoft Teams, Abuse AD CS to Steal Company Data
articles.summary:
Attackers posing as IT support on Microsoft Teams talked employees into giving them remote control of their PCs. They then used insecure Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) settings to obtain login certificates for privileged accounts, including one for a domain controller.
Microsoft said in a report that it investigated two such intrusions, one of which resulted in company data being copied to an external server.
The attackers exploited no flaw in Teams itself. They relied on social engineering and on AD CS that had been set up insecurely, and Microsoft did not tie the activity to any known group.
How the Attacks Began
Both intrusions started the same way, Microsoft said. The attackers messaged and called employees on Teams while posing as the company's own IT or help desk, working from outside tenants with support-themed names so the contact looked familiar.
They talked each user into opening Quick Assist, a remote-help tool built into Windows, and reading the connection code back to them. That gave the attacker direct, hands-on control of the workstation.
From there, the attacker dropped an archive into the Downloads folder, unpacked it into a new folder named to resemble a Windows update, and ran its contents with a portable Python, Bun, or Java runtime. File names alone were a weak signal, because one copy was renamed while still carrying the real runtime's version details.

El cielo de “La noche estrellada” parece responder a una noche concreta. Por ejemplo, el 22 de julio de 1889 en Saint-Rémy-de-Provence (sur de Francia). Un equipo surcoreano ha analizado el cielo que representa y lo ha comparado con el real de aquel verano. Se trata de la mejor opción que han encontrado. Es decir, que era el cielo que podía verse entonces, pero eso no implica que fuera el día en el que pintó el cuadro.
En el estudio publicado en Scientific Reports (22 de octubre de 2026) proponen una revisión de la cronología habitual. También que Venus ocupa una posición concreta y que las Híades (un grupo de estrellas de la constelación de Tauro) están juntas. Todo ello es consistente con amaneceres cercanos al 22 de julio. 								By: Technical Paper Link
								
							
Researchers at imec and Vrije Universiteit Brussels published “Embodied Emissions of 2.5D and 3D Scaling in Chipletized GPUs for Low-Carbon AI.”
Abstract
“GPU compute resources are scaling to support growing AI workloads, leading to further rises in the climate change impact of hyperscale data centers that rely on high-performance GPUs. To model how packaging decisions impact the carbon footprint we have estimated the embodied emissions (EE) of a chiplet-based GPU that has been scaled in 2.5D and 3D using the imec netzero modeling platform. We doubled the number of compute units and high bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity in the 2.5D and 3D scaled systems and found that 3D scaling results in an 89% increase in EE, as compared to an increase of 141% for 2.5D scaling, positioning 3D scaling as an attractive solution to limit the embodied emissions due to GPU scaling.”

articles.title: Stablecoins will not become mainstream by one company

Stablecoins are moving beyond crypto trading to become part of how African businesses move money across borders, panellists said at Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos.
The session, “The New Payment Backbone”, brought together Mercy Emmanuel, stablecoin and blockchain vertical lead at Flutterwave; Tayo Oviosu, group CEO of Paga; and Ife Johnson, co-founder and CEO of Juicyway. Vivian Mbene, chief operating officer of Breet, moderated.
The case for stablecoins starts with speed. A payment from Lagos to Nairobi has often travelled through correspondent banks in New York or London, taking days to clear and stopping for weekends and bank holidays. Stablecoins, digital tokens pegged to currencies such as the US dollar, skip those stops.
“Stablecoins essentially collapse this journey, as a high-speed train would,” Emmanuel said. “Settlement happens in seconds; it happens in minutes.”
Oviosu said customers care about the result. They want payments that are fast, cheap and arrive when promised, and most will never know a stablecoin was involved. Building stablecoins into everyday payment systems, he said, makes cross-border transfers simpler without asking users to learn anything new.
He also said the industry will have to build it together. “No one company is going to solve it on their own,” he said. “There are going to be multiple companies that have specific solutions that will target different audiences.”

articles.title: Google finds 'LLMjacking' attackers running up $100K a day in fraudulent cloud charges - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Google finds ‘LLMjacking’ attackers running up $100K a day in fraudulent cloud charges
A new report out today from Google LLC’s Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group finds that attackers who hijack enterprise access to large language models are running up fraudulent cloud charges of more than $100,000 in a single day.
The report, “The Rise of LLMJacking: How Threat Actors Monetize Compromised Cloud and Model Resources,” covers multiple LLMjacking cases Mandiant responded to this year. At some organizations, the cumulative bill reached $1 million before access was revoked.
Cryptojacking, the older way of stealing cloud compute, tends to drain resources gradually. LLMjacking charges can spike in a matter of hours.
Victims in North America, South America and Asia-Pacific included financial services and retail companies, along with technology and transportation businesses. GTIG has tied the intrusions to several financially motivated clusters and sees a growing split between the people who break in and the operators who resell the access.

U.S. data centers use 17 to 19 billion gallons of water to cool their hot-running chips each year — and that number is expected to triple in the next five years, according to The Water Foundation.

Omen AI was founded in 2024 to solve that problem. The company is building a real-time sensor to determine whether valves were failing, or if bacteria growth in the system threatened to choke off water flow. After raising a $31 million Series A in June, Omen is now acquiring competitor Aquatic Labs in a $16 million cash-and-stock deal.
The deal came together after Omen founder Zach Laberge was introduced to Aquatic Labs’ CEO Allan Adams by an investor in the filtration space. Putting those two technologies in the same sensor creates a “much richer picture of the water and the fluid,” Adams told TechCrunch, while uniting their vision of automating what had previously been a slow, manual process.

articles.title: Stablecoins in Africa are held back by spending
articles.summary:
Stablecoins already move money in and out of Africa faster and more cheaply than banks. What keeps them from the mainstream is that people still can’t spend them easily, and regulators still can’t see where they go.
That was the view from “The Adoption Gap”, a panel at Moonshot by TechCabal on Thursday, October 29. Shalom Osiadi, founder and CEO of Esca Finance, a foreign exchange company serving businesses in emerging markets, and Demilade Olugbenga, B2B business development manager at Breet, a Nigerian crypto payments platform, discussed with moderator Nnanna Ijezie why adoption still lags.
“Some people use stablecoins, but they’re not able to spend them in the applications they use daily,” Olugbenga said. “Say I’m a freelancer and someone wants to pay me in stablecoins. If I look around and there’s no stablecoin option, I will tell whoever is paying me, ‘Sorry, I can’t accept this now.’”
Sub-Saharan Africa received more than $205 billion in on-chain crypto value between July 2024 and June 2025, with Nigeria taking in $92.1 billion, according to Chainalysis. Stablecoins made up about 43% of the region’s crypto volume over that period.
Olugbenga said sending anything from $5 to $500,000 on Breet costs 10 cents, while a bank transfer can take days and eat up to 8% of the amount. Banks charge that much, Osiadi said, because African currencies can move before a transfer lands, so they build wide margins into their exchange rates.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has taken to X, the social network that he owns, to mock OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's stance that it's "quite terrible" for home computer users to have DRAM in their machines. "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5% of the time," Altman said during the YouTube interview. CEO and co-founder of StackBlitz, the parent company of Bolt.new.

In a nutshell: Google's struggles with Android fragmentation are well documented and date back more than a decade. The subject hasn't come up in a while, however, naturally leading some to believe that the issue has gradually resolved itself. It turns out that's not the case.
According to the latest Android distribution figures, Android 17 – the latest version of the mobile OS – is installed on just 0.9% of devices worldwide. Android 16 owns the lion's share of distribution at 25.4%, followed by Android 15 with a 14.7% stake. Android 13, which shipped way back in the summer of 2022, is still installed on 11.8% of devices, while 9.6% of users are clinging to Android 12.
For comparison, around 15% of Apple mobile users are running a version of iOS 27 and nearly half are using a variant of iOS 26, according to StatCounter.
Why the disparity between Android and iOS adoption, you ask? Well, it largely comes down to distribution and who controls what.
With iOS, Apple develops its hardware and software under a single roof. This means Cupertino controls when new updates go out and what devices can get them. Over at Google, when a new version of Android is ready, it gets sent out to device partners that often like to spend additional time applying tweaks in the form of overlays and skins. Customizing the OS is a great way to differentiate your product from others on the market, but also burns the clock. Obiex says Nigeria’s stablecoin market is far more efficient than it was in 2018 and 2019, when the gap between buying and selling a dollar of crypto in naira ran as wide as ₦20 to ₦30. Demand has scaled since, but the supply behind it is still spread across many small sellers.
That’s the current state of Nigeria’s stablecoin market, according to Temitayo Sadique, managing director of Obiex Business, the business arm of Nigerian crypto exchange Obiex.

Scattered supply makes that volume expensive to move. A company filling a $1 million order might deal with 10 peer-to-peer (P2P) traders, Sadique said, each selling a slice at a slightly higher rate: ₦1,400 per dollar, then ₦1,402, then ₦1,403. By the end, its average price is worse than the first quote. As volumes grow, he argued, platforms that can fill large orders at one price will set the terms for everyone else.

articles.summary:
A botnet of more than 1.3 million Android devices, mostly TV set-top boxes, lost control of its servers in late October in a takedown led by Google.
Google says it is highly confident that device maker Videostrong intentionally put a backdoor in the boxes and sold access to criminals.
They used the boxes for ad fraud and to pass other people's internet traffic through owners' home connections. The backdoor is still on the boxes, and owners cannot remove it themselves.
Videostrong, based in Shenzhen, China, makes Android TV boxes and other devices under its own name and for other brands. The backdoor, called x.cpe, was built into many device models and brands over several years. Google does not believe a rogue insider or a mistake was to blame.
Google used legal action to take down the domains and servers that controlled the botnet. It also took down the control domains of more than a dozen malware families loaded through the backdoor. Japan's National Police Agency, Lumen, HUMAN Security, Plume, Synthient and TrendAI worked with Google on the operation.
Because the criminals behind that malware also spread it in other ways, Google expects the action to cut off their access to at least 10 million more infected devices. It warns that backdoor operators and the criminals who buy from them quickly switch to new tools when one part of their setup is disrupted.
Google has cut ties with Videostrong. It banned the company, and any future subsidiaries or affiliates, from building or s…

articles.title: 42AI comes out of stealth with $62.5M and a world model that can 'predict human behavior' | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Here’s a question straight out of sci-fi: What if AI could predict what you were going to do before you decided to, even in a completely new situation?
Israeli startup 42AI says it is developing a “behavioral world model” that can do just that, and it has just come out of stealth with $62.5 million in seed funding. The company is initially running its predictive system at a handful of financial brokerages, where it says the model can help predict how individual traders will respond to volatile conditions.
“Behavior is not deterministic; it’s constantly probabilistic,” 42AI’s CEO and co-founder Amit Gal-Or told TechCrunch when I asked him to justify his company’s tall claim. He argues that people have underlying psychological tendencies that influence their decisions even when their circumstances change, and that’s what the startup is trying to measure and convert into data that the model can understand.
“A week from now, you might be a different person, but your tendencies will always play out in certain areas to a probability or distribution,” his co-founder and CTO Ehud Ezra added. And that, the company argues, is what the model does: show the probability of a person making a certain decision.
42AI says the model tries to figure out people’s internal motivations instead of extrapolating patterns based on their previous actions. To do that, 42AI examines how people react to seemingly unrelated events. For an investor or trader, for example, such events might include completi…

articles.title: NASA's Swift Space Telescope is set to crash back to Earth this week
articles.summary:
Don't Look Up: After spending more than 20 years in space, the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory is now expected to undergo a "catastrophic" reentry into Earth's atmosphere. Most of the telescope should burn up during the process, but a few surviving pieces could eventually reach the ground and pose a risk to people.
The Swift Observatory could plunge back to Earth as early as this Friday, US authorities said. The telescope is expected to undergo an uncontrolled reentry after NASA and Katalyst Space Technologies tried – and failed – to correct the spacecraft's orbit using a robotic device in September.
According to US Space Force predictions, the Swift Observatory should burn up in the atmosphere during reentry. A few components, including tungsten-made parts and mirrors, might survive the atmospheric plunge and eventually reach the ground.
The Space Force is tracking Swift's orbit to determine where these components could land. Parts of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, Central America, and South America could potentially be affected. Most likely, however, the surviving debris will end up in the ocean.
According to John Nousek, an astronomer at Pennsylvania State University who is in charge of Swift's control team, the aging telescope is going down with a bang.
"We've known this day would come since before Swift was launched. At least in low-Earth orbit, what goes up must come down," Nousek said.

articles.title: Una nueva oeada de ciberataques hace que las neveras suban hasta 50 grados. Está pasando en Bélgica y Suecia
articles.summary:
Tener los dispositivos conectados permite su gestión centralizada y a distancia. Esto supone una enorme ventaja para las empresas con miles de estos dispositivos desperdigados, por eso las grandes cadenas de supermercados centralizan controles como el de la refrigeración de sus productos. El problema llega cuando el acceso al sistema no está suficientemente bien protegido: un ciberataque arruinó toneladas de productos en Francia.
Calor en las neveras del norte. Tras el grave problema que se desencadenó en Francia, donde los supermercados se vieron perjudicados, Suecia y Bélgica están viviendo un episodio similar: los frigoríficos de algunas grandes cadenas de alimentación vieron elevada su temperatura hasta llegar a límites de 50 ºC.
El incidente comenzó a afectar el pasado domingo por la noche en las tiendas de los países mencionados. La mecánica ha sido similar a la de Francia: repentinamente, los frigoríficos variaron su temperatura de frío sin que los operarios alterasen dicha temperatura. Aunque en un principio se hablaba de un fallo informático, actualmente son varios los medios que lo denominan ciberataque.
Dispositivos expuestos. Si en Francia se descubrió que el acceso a determinadas neveras Danfoss utilizaban "admin" como usuario de administración y el día como código de contraseña para acceder al sistema, aún no se sabe cuál ha sido el vector de intrusión en este nuevo ataque. articles.title: ChatGPT subit des perturbations : ce que l'on sait de la panne en cours — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Les signalements ont commencé à grimper sur Downdetector vers 17 h 30 (heure de Paris) ce lundi 2 novembre. Les utilisateurs décrivent une page qui tourne dans le vide ou une réponse qui s’arrête au milieu d’une phrase. De notre côté, rien de tel, le service fonctionne chez nous.
Néanmoins, une panne de ChatGPT touche vite beaucoup de monde, même quand elle est partielle : le chatbot d’OpenAI a dépassé le milliard d’utilisateurs chaque semaine.
Cloudflare en cause ?
Le site indien PaidFreeDroid a publié une explication vers 19 heures, heure de Paris. Selon lui, le réseau de Cloudflare marcherait à moitié alors que les serveurs d’OpenAI qui font tourner les modèles fonctionneraient normalement.
En revanche, certains relais de Cloudflare perdraient des données en route, en Inde, en Amérique du Nord et en Europe, et afficheraient des pages d’erreur 520, 522 ou 524.
ChatGPT peut aussi sembler fonctionner en envoyant sa réponse mot après mot, en continu, et si la connexion lâche en cours de route, le texte se coupe net ou se répète.
Ce genre de panne est déjà arrivé. Le 18 novembre 2025, une panne de Cloudflare avait coupé ChatGPT, X ou Shopify pendant plusieurs heures. Selon CNBC, la page de statut d’OpenAI avait alors attribué ses problèmes à un « fournisseur de services tiers ».

articles.title: Jevons’ Paradox and the Silicon Roadmap - EE Times
articles.summary:
AI usage may expand with more efficient models and hardware, just as Jevons would predict. But the silicon roadmap adds a layer of complexity to the market prediction.
Gartner vs Jevons
A couple of weeks ago, Gartner published a forecast that raises concerns about AI infrastructure. AI providers will spend close to $1 trillion on infrastructure in 2026 and another $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030. To pay for that, cover the cost of borrowing, and still earn a 12% return, the owners of AI data centers would need about $8.5 trillion in revenue through 2030. Gartner expects the AI revenue that actually reaches those data centers to be $3.6 trillion at most. On that arithmetic, says Gartner, more than $3.5 trillion of this spending could be exposed to write-downs by 2030, and more than 80% of neoclouds will no longer exist as independent companies. That is a risk estimate under Gartner’s assumptions, not a prediction that the full amount will be written off.
On the other hand, IMHO, this math assumes that AI will continue to be deployed in a similar use and business model as today. However, we might well be only at the beginning of the AI use curve. And, according to the by-now very well-known Jevons paradox, the more a technology is available, the more people will find new use-models for that technology, and therefore, even if the technology price goes down, the revenue from the aggregated usage can go up. articles.title: Panique sur l'iPhone : Apple met en garde contre une opération d'espionnage dans 99 pays, dont la France
articles.summary:
Apple tire de nouveau la sonnette d’alarme. Le 29 octobre, le géant de Cupertino a envoyé une nouvelle vague de notifications à des utilisateurs d’iPhone dans le viseur de logiciels espions. Selon Apple, leurs smartphones ont été pris pour cible par un logiciel espion dit « mercenaire ». Il s’agit d’un outil de surveillance coûteux, généralement vendu à des gouvernements étrangers, comme la Chine, la Corée du Nord ou la Russie.
Des députés allemands dans le viseur
En Allemagne, l’alerte émise par Apple a pris une tournure politique. L’Office fédéral de la sécurité des systèmes d’information (BSI) a prévenu des membres du parlement fédéral et du gouvernement que leurs iPhone avaient peut-être été visés par un virus.
« Il s’agit pour l’instant de pure spéculation, il faut attendre de savoir de quoi il s’agit concrètement. Mais c’est évidemment quelque chose qui nous préoccupe beaucoup », a déclaré le ministre du Numérique allemand, Karsten Wildberger.
Par précaution, le BSI recommande aux destinataires de considérer que leur appareil a été compromis. Il faut donc s’en débarrasser et, surtout, éviter les communications sensibles sur l’appareil. Le type de logiciel espion qui provoque des alertes Apple peut en effet lire les messages, y compris sur les messageries chiffrées, accéder aux appels, aux contacts, à l’agenda et à la localisation… et même activer le micro et la caméra. Le malware peut donc récupérer en peu de temps énormément d’informations sensibles.

articles.title: Andes Waits For Market Momentum For Cuzco CPU - EE Times
articles.summary:
TAIPEI, Taiwan – Andes Technology has slowed development of its Cuzco high-end RISC-V CPU IP as it redirects engineering resources to a rapidly growing AI business, CTO Charlie Su told EE Times. Su insisted the project’s ambition remains, even if the technology emerges in a different form and on a different timeline than originally planned.
RISC-V IP vendor Andes had spun out Condor to develop Cuzco after identifying a future market need for a high-end data center CPU based on RISC-V, but pulled the technology back in-house earlier this year.
“The ecosystem needs to gradually go there before you have the hardware, otherwise you cannot catch the opportunity,” Su said. “We started, but as time went on, we found the AI part of our business continued to grow very strongly.”
Andes’s AI business currently accounts for half of its revenue, growing 30% last year and likely to grow 50% this year, Su said, which will require additional resources internally. Andes has a small deep learning accelerator (up to around 4 TOPS at 1 GHz) with its own compiler, but most of its revenue in AI comes from AI chip companies using Andes CPU cores for control, orchestration, and data movement (including Meta, d-Matrix, Fractile, and Axelera). Many of these licenses are for custom cores, and delivery schedules can be extremely demanding, Su said.
“We decided to consolidate and slow down [Cuzco], so we could put more resources on the immediate revenue generation part,” he said.

articles.title: Novas regras de SAC entram em vigor no Brasil; veja o que muda • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Novas regras de SAC entram em vigor no Brasil; veja o que muda
Regulamento inclui atendimento humano dentro de até 20 segundos para 80% das chamadas, quando o cliente solicitar.
Começaram a valer, nesta segunda-feira (02/11), as novas regras de SAC (Serviço de Atendimento ao Consumidor) do Brasil. A principal mudança determina que pelo menos 80% das ligações a serviços do tipo sejam atendidas por pessoas em até 20 segundos, quando solicitado pelo cliente.
Baseadas no Decreto nº 13.135, de 9 de outubro de 2026, as novas regras entram em vigor 20 dias depois de terem sido publicadas no Diário Oficial da União e, com isso, revogam o Decreto nº 11.034, de 5 de abril de 2022, vigente até então.
O objetivo do novo decreto é aprimorar e padronizar os serviços de atendimento ao cliente oferecidos por empresas de setores regulados pelo governo federal, como operadoras de telecomunicações, fornecedoras de energia elétrica, bancos e companhias aéreas.
A principal mudança é a que foi descrita já no início do texto: pelo menos 80% dos atendimentos prestados a pessoas que entrarem em contato por telefone deverão ser prestados por um humano, se solicitado, em até 20 segundos; para o restante das demandas, o atendimento humano deverá ser oferecido em até cinco minutos.
O atendimento telefônico deve ser oferecido, no mínimo, entre 8:00 e 20:00, todos os dias da semana. Se a chamada for interrompida antes da conclusão do atendimento, a empresa deverá retornar a ligação em até cinco minutos.

articles.title: Electra avait promis de ne pas toucher aux anciens forfaits de recharge : 6 mois plus tard, c'est raté
articles.summary:
En matière de recharge rapide pour voitures électriques, la réputation se construit lentement sur la fiabilité des bornes et le maillage du réseau, mais elle peut se fissurer beaucoup plus vite pour des histoires d’argent. articles.title: En Ibiza hay un pueblo que se debate entre el turismo de borrachera y de lujo. Su mayor problema es otro: el precio de la vivienda
articles.summary:
Sant Antoni de Portmany es un municipio situado en la cara oeste de la isla de Ibiza. Poco más de 29.000 vecinos, playas idílicas, yates, sol y fiesta. Un lugar ideal para unas buenas vacaciones en el Mediterráneo. El problema es que sus habitantes se han visto atrapados por una pinza que no es ajena a otros enclaves del litoral: la zona está viendo cómo su oferta hotelera apuesta cada vez más por el turismo de lujo, una forma de sacudirse la imagen de destino de excesos y borracheras. Más o menos igual que Magaluf, en Mallorca.
Sin embargo, de momento lo que se han encontrado sus habitantes es otra cosa: una vivienda a precios intocables.
Un “pueblo atrapado”. La expresión no es nuestra. La usa elDiario.es en un amplio artículo en el que analiza la peculiar situación a la que ha llegado Sant Antoni de Portmany, una localidad del litoral ibicenco que se ve condicionada por tres factores: turismo de borrachera, turismo de lujo y un encarecimiento residencial mayúsculo que, asegura el digital, lo convierte en el municipio con “la mayor subida en los precios de la vivienda de Ibiza”.
De fondo, un dilema espinoso: ¿Cómo cambiar la imagen de un destino tras años asociado a los excesos, el turismo hooligan y la fiesta? ¿Y cómo hacerlo sin agravar la crisis residencial que arrastra en general Ibiza y obliga a parte de sus trabajadores (incluidos los que mantienen a flote los restaurantes y hoteles) a vivir en parques de caravanas?

articles.title: The in-store telemetry blackout costing retailers billions
articles.summary:
The in-store telemetry blackout costing retailers billions
Real-time payment telemetry and AI prevent costly checkout failures
Walk into the network operations center of any major enterprise and you will see an array of monitoring capability. Massive dashboards track API response times to the millisecond and map digital customer journeys from an ad click on a smartphone all the way to a virtual shopping basket. On paper, enterprise IT has achieved total operational awareness.
AVP of Observability and Performance at FreedomPay.
Step onto the high street at twelve-thirty on a Friday afternoon, however, and that illusion dissolves. A payment terminal freezes at a busy cafe counter. The line extends out the door. The cashier tries rebooting the hardware while office workers check their watches.
Within minutes, shoppers begin walking out empty-handed, heading straight for the competitor across the street. Back at corporate headquarters, central monitoring dashboards remain entirely green. As far as IT knows, systems are operating normally.
This disconnect represents one of the most significant operational blind spots in physical commerce today. In the UK alone, checkout failures put an estimated £1.7 billion in annual sales at risk. When transactions stall during peak trading windows, that revenue is cannot be recovered.
The failure is rarely a collapse of the central cloud. Often, it is a telemetry blackout occurring at the critical physical touchpoint where money actually change…

articles.title: This Halloween, make sure your sensitive data Is wearing a mask
articles.summary:
This Halloween, make sure your sensitive data Is wearing a mask
Protecting sensitive data as AI access expands
If you work in cybersecurity for long enough, you learn that we really love an analogy or a metaphor and come October you can barely move for talk of security nightmares, cyber monsters and threats lurking in the shadows.
I enjoy a good analogy as much as anyone, but there’s one Halloween comparison I don't hear very often. And, for data security at least, I think it might be the most useful one right now: the mask.
A mask doesn't make what's underneath disappear. It simply means you don't have to reveal its true identity to everyone who encounters it, and that’s what we’re trying to achieve with sensitive data.
VP of Data Security Products at cybersecurity company Thales.
Developers need data to test applications, analysts need it to find patterns, and AI tools and agents increasingly need access to enterprise information to do useful work. But needing to use this data isn't necessarily the same as needing to see every sensitive value it contains.
That's precisely where data masking comes in. By replacing sensitive information with realistic but unusable values, organizations can preserve the usefulness of data without unnecessarily exposing what's underneath.
With AI dramatically increasing where data can travel, who can find it and what can act upon it, that distinction is becoming much more important.

articles.title: Cyberattaque sur les frigos de supermarchés : après la France, des pirates s'attaquent à d'autres pays d'Europe
articles.summary:

Les attaquants ont activé le mode dégivrage des installations. De facto, la température s’est mise à grimper dans les frigos et les congélateurs, mettant en danger les denrées qui y sont stockées.

Dans certains magasins, la température des frigos et des surgélateurs avait grimpé jusqu’à 15 °C. articles.title: Un robot de reparto provoca un accidente con nueve heridos en Tallin y sigue su camino: técnicamente, es un conductor a la fuga
articles.summary:
Eran casi las seis de la tarde en una concurrida vía del centro de Tallin por la que circulaba un autobús urbano lleno de pasajeros. De repente, algo se cruzó en el camino y el conductor se vio obligado a dar un frenazo brusco que mandó al suelo a varios pasajeros que iban de pie. Quien lo provocó siguió tranquilamente su camino sin mirar atrás.
El culpable de este incidente no tiene ni carnet de conducir ni DNI: es un robot de reparto autónomo que cruzó la calle con el semáforo en rojo y causó el accidente. Ahora la policía de Estonia lo investiga, y Europa se topa con una pregunta para la que todavía no tiene una respuesta clara: ¿quién responde cuando el causante de un accidente es una máquina autónoma?
Un cruce en rojo y nueve heridos. Según informaba la empresa municipal de transporte TLT, el lunes 26 de octubre, un robot de reparto autónomo de Bolt llegó a un paso de peatones y, sin pensárselo dos veces, cruzó la calle con el semáforo en rojo. El conductor de un autobús que circulaba con el semáforo en verse, se vio obligado a frenar de golpe. Como consecuencia, varios pasajeros que iban de pie cayeron y hasta nueve personas resultaron heridas a causa de la caída.
El vídeo del autobús muestra el choque y cómo el robot es empujado por la calzada para luego seguir su camino como si nada hubiese sucedido. MobiKwik’s revenue grew 9.4% in Q2 FY27, driven by higher gross merchandise value (GMV) and improved margins.
MobiKwik reported a net profit in the second quarter of FY27, compared with a loss in the year-ago period, marking its fourth consecutive profitable quarter and its highest-ever quarterly profit.

Revenue rose 9.4% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 295.70 crore. MobiKwik attributed the quarter’s performance to higher gross merchandise value (GMV) growth and improved margins.
“We believe that the operating leverage in our business model will compound as we evolve into an AI-first company. Our continued focus on cost optimisation and operating efficiency is further strengthening our operating model and will drive profitability as we scale,” said Bipin Preet Singh, MD & CEO, MobiKwik.
According to MobiKwik, its payment business recorded a 35% year-on-year (YoY) growth in gross merchandise value (GMV) to Rs 59,677 crore in Q2 FY27. Consumer payments GMV grew 27% YoY to Rs 46,375 crore, while lending disbursals rose 34% to Rs 1,082.6 crore during the quarter.
The company’s registered user base increased to 196.3 million in Q2 FY27, compared with 183.5 million in the corresponding quarter last fiscal.

articles.title: L'armée française vient de recevoir un Rafale pas comme les autres, qui va préparer le futur Rafale F5
articles.summary:
La Direction générale de l'armement a livré à son centre DGA Essais en vol son premier Rafale avion banc d'essais. Désigné B374, ce laboratoire volant servira à tester les équipements et armements du futur Rafale F5.
Le ministère des Armées, par le biais de la Direction générale de l'armement (DGA), a annoncé ce lundi 2 novembre la livraison du premier Rafale avion banc d'essais (ABE) au centre DGA Essais en vol. Construit par Dassault Aviation et livré au standard F4.1, l'appareil sera progressivement transformé d'ici 2028 pour accueillir une instrumentation de vol complète. Il deviendra alors la plateforme d'essais des futurs équipements du Rafale F5, dont le radar de nouvelle génération RBE2 XG.
Ce Rafale n’ira pas en escadron, il va servir de laboratoire volant au futur Rafale F5
Un avion dit « banc d'essais », c'est en quelque sorte un laboratoire avec des ailes. Pour ce qui est du Rafale, l'appareil est modifié en profondeur pour embarquer des instruments de mesure et des enregistreurs qui collectent les données pendant le vol, un peu comme une boîte noire, mais en beaucoup plus bavard. Grâce à une liaison de données, ces informations parviennent aussi aux ingénieurs qui conduisent les essais depuis le sol. Qu'il s'agisse de la navigation, des systèmes d'attaque, des capteurs, des armements, des communications ou des logiciels de bord, chaque nouvelle technologie peut ainsi être éprouvée en vol, en conditions réelles.

articles.title: In one of the largest deals in tech history, Marvell buys Lumentum for $115B | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Custom chip designer Marvell has signed a deal to acquire optical chip and networking equipment maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal with an enterprise value of $115 billion (including debt) and an equity value of about $80 billion. Marvell will provide 4.5 shares of its common stock for each share of Lumentum.
This makes the deal one of the biggest acquisitions in tech history. It compares to Microsoft buying Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion in 2022 and Dell buying EMC for $67 billion in 2016.
Interestingly, the two companies have one major shareholder in common: Nvidia. In March, as part of a multi-year agreement to purchase Lumentum’s advanced laser components, the GPU giant invested $2 billion to support Lumentum’s R&D efforts and fab expansion. Later that same month, Marvell announced that Nvidia invested $2 billion in an effort to beef up Marvell’s optical networking and chips portfolio.
With Lumentum, Marvell says it will become a leader in AI connectivity, with products that range from chips to data centers. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of calendar year 2028, should both companies’ shareholders, and regulators, agree.

articles.title: Qualcomm Validates HBC Silicon, Samples Appear in First Half of 2027
articles.summary:
Monday, November 2nd 2026
Qualcomm Validates HBC Silicon, Samples Appear in First Half of 2027
Qualcomm has officially validated its High Bandwidth Compute (HBC) concept, which the company showcased this summer. Instead of using traditional HBM and compute dies, Qualcomm has developed a technology that stacks multiple LPDDR layers and embeds a base die that serves as a compute engine for AI inference. In Qualcomm's San Diego lab, the first-generation HBC has achieved silicon validation with full read-write and near-memory computation capabilities. HBC utilizes LPDDR memory, stacking it across multiple layers in a 3D vertical space and interconnecting them with through-silicon vias (TSVs). This approach provides better energy efficiency than traditional HBM, which stacks regular DDR in vertical layers, as the low-power DDR (LPDDR) chips consume less power while delivering similar bandwidth and capacity.
Qualcomm has successfully stacked multiple LPDDR layers on top of each other, with the base of the HBC being a compute die that performs near-memory computation and offloads processing to near-memory dies. This technique is similar to what HBM4 memory currently does, with the base die being a logic die to better integrate compute solutions for packet tracing and data preparation for entering and exiting HBM. articles.title: Most users can now upgrade to Windows 11 26H2, even from Windows 10
articles.summary:
TL;DR: A few weeks into the rollout, Microsoft has confirmed that all eligible Windows users can now get the latest OS build on their compatible systems. There are no earth-shattering changes this time, but the extra security bonus should be enticing enough for most people.
Microsoft recently updated its official guidance on installing the latest version of Windows 11. Windows 11, version 26H2 is now available to all eligible devices, including those running the 25H2 and 24H2 releases and, well, most everything else a reasonably modern PC can run. The upgrade process also supports the latest Windows 10 version enrolled in the extended support program.
Windows 10 reached its scheduled end of life in 2025, but Microsoft has repeatedly extended the window for customers who want to hang on a bit longer. The highlander of operating systems can now receive free, officially sanctioned security updates for home users until October 2027. Beyond funding: Why every startup founder needs an insurance plan
From personal term insurance to keyman and employee cover, here's how insurance solutions can help entrepreneurs protect their families, businesses, and teams.
Most founders are equity-rich and cash-poor, with household finances quietly tied to the venture: personal guarantees on business loans, savings deployed into the company, a spouse’s income covering monthly basics. That structure makes personal term insurance more urgent for a founder than for a salaried peer, not less. If the founder dies, the family inherits illiquid equity and live liabilities at the same moment, and only a large, immediate payout resolves that.
The sizing rule also needs adjusting. The standard guidance of 10-15X annual income understates the need for entrepreneurs who deliberately pay themselves a modest salary. Anchor instead to household expenses, outstanding personal guarantees, and the real cost of the family’s next 15 years. Self-employed applicants should expect income documentation requests, ITRs, and bank statements rather than salary slips, and treat that as an administrative step rather than a reason to postpone.

articles.summary:
Snap has reached a settlement in a lawsuit brought by two teenagers who accused the company of designing its platform to be addictive and contributing to their depression, anxiety, and eating disorders, as first reported by Reuters. The plaintiffs had previously reached settlements with Meta, TikTok, and YouTube.
The trial was set to be Snap’s first in a broader wave of litigation over social media’s impact on young users. The company had already settled its other cases scheduled for trial. Snap CEO Evan Spiegel was expected to take the stand.
The plaintiffs said they started using YouTube as young as age 3 and other social media platforms at around age 9. They said they developed compulsive usage habits, which they attributed to features such as autoplay and infinite scrolling.
“The Parties are pleased to have been able to resolve this matter in an amicable manner,” a Snap spokesperson said in a statement to TechCrunch. “We’ve built safeguards, launched safety tutorials, and partnered with experts and because safety is never finished, we remain committed to continually strengthening the safety, privacy, and well-being of our community.”
Social media giants are facing thousands of lawsuits in federal and state courts over claims that they knowingly designed their platforms to hook young users and fuel a youth mental health crisis involving anxiety, depression, and suicide.

Project takes a stock Qwen 3.5 4B and compiles a RISC-V CPU into its weights.
AI engineer Divyansh Agrawal has revealed the Qwenputer. Described in its most basic terms, Qwenputer is an experimental blend of the stock Qwen 3.5 4B AI LLM with a 32-bit RISC-V CPU compiled and inserted directly into its weights. In use, Qwenputer can run processor arithmetic operations – or even run C and MicroPython code on its built-in CPU, eschewing any external runtime or tool use. Moreover, it can run Doom, albeit very slowly. You can see the Qwenputer running Doom on its RISC-V CPU by expanding the tweet below.
The implementation of Qwenputer raises some interesting concepts and solutions. For example, the developer used Qwen’s Gated DeltaNet (GND) state as RAM, which Agrawal reckons is “a pretty neat trick.” They admit that using these ‘fast weights’ as RAM isn’t an original concept, but modifying Qwen 3.5 this way does seem to be a first.
Unlike traditional LLM creation, adding a ‘CPU’ doesn’t involve training. This RISC-V CPU implementation “is 11 transformer layers in front of Qwen's own, and none of their weights are learned: a compiler computes every one,” it is explained. articles.title: New York Times and other outlets sue web browser Brave over alleged content scraping | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The New York Times sued Brave, the 11-year-old, privacy-focused browser company, on Monday, alleging it scraped the outlet’s copyrighted content and unlawfully distributed it to customers the suit names as Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere.
Separately on Monday, the Daily News, the Chicago Tribune, and the Orlando Sentinel filed a similar lawsuit. Both were brought in federal court in Manhattan.
The New York Times, which has also sued OpenAI and Perplexity over similar claims, likens Brave to a “supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content” for AI companies.
“In this way, Brave acts both like a burglar that misappropriates the content of publishers, and an AI ‘fence’ that sells stolen content to third parties,” the suit reads. It says Brave built an index of more than 30 billion web pages using an unidentified crawler, leaving publishers unable to block it.
The suit also targets a Brave browser feature that bypasses paywalls and the company’s practice of blocking publishers’ ads while selling its own.
Founded in 2015, Brave has raised roughly $250 million to date, according to private-market trackers. The Times seeks an injunction and damages.
Brave did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
